OFFICIAL NOTE from Lord Grenville to the Minister for Foreign Affairs, at , dated January 20th, 1800.

The Official Note transmitted by the Minister for Foreign Affairs in France, and received by the underfilled on the 18th Infiant, has been laid before the King.

His Majesty cannot forbear expressing the Concern with which he observes in that Note that the unprovoked Aggrdfions of France, the foie Cause and Origin of the War, are systematically defended by her present Rulers, 'under the same injurious Pretences by which they were originally attempted to be disguised. His Majesty will not enter into the Refutation of Allegations now uni-verfally exploded, and (in lb far as they respect His Majesty's Conduct) not only in themselves utterly groundless,.but contradicted both by the internal Evidence of the Transactions to which they relate, and also by the express Testimpny (given at the Time) of the Govern-tnent of France itself.

With respect to the Object of the Note, His Majesty can only refer to the Answer which He has already given.

He. his explained, without Reserve, the Obstades which in His Judgment preclude, at the present Moment, all Hope of Advantage from Negotiation. All the Inducements to treat which are relied upon in the French Official Note; the Personal Dispositions which are said to prevail for the Conclusion of Peace, and for the future Observance of Treaties; the Tower of insuring the Effect of those Dispositions, supposing them to exist; and the Solidity and Consistency of the System newly established after so rapid a Succession of Resolutions: — All these, are Points which can be known only from that Test to which His Majesty has already referred them; the Rel'ult of Experience, and the Evidence of Fads.

With that Sincerity and Plainness which His Anxiety for the Re-establishment of Peace indispensably required, His Majesty has pointed out to France the surest and speediest Means for the Attainment of that great Object. But He has declared, in Terms equally explicit, and with the same Sincerity, that He entertains no Desire to prescribe to a Foreign Nation the Form of its Government; that he looks«only to the Security of His own Dominions, and of Europe; and that, whenever that essential Object can in His Judgment be in any Manner whatever sufficiently provided for, He will eagerly concert with His Allies the Means of immediate and joint Negotiation for the Re-establishment of general Tran-, quillity.

To these Declarations His Majesty steadily adheres; and it is only on the Grounds thus stated, that His Regard to the Safety of His Subjects will fuller Him to renounce that System of vigorous Defence, to which,

3 *

II5 *

under the Favour of Providence, His Kingdoms owe the Security of those Blessings which they now enjoy.

(Signed), Grenville.

Downing Street,

The Orders of the Day being read, for taking into, Consideration His Majesty's Most Gracious Message of Wednesday last; and also, the several Papers which were that Day presented to the House by Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer, by His Majesty's Command;

And then the House adjourned till Tomorrow Morning, Ten of the Clock.

Prohibited Fa ft India Goods.

Mart is, 28° di Januarii;

Anno 40 Georgii IIIUi Regis, 1800. Prayers.

THE House being informed, that some of the Commissioners of the Customs attended at the Door, they were called in; and at the Bar, presented to the House, pursuant to the Directions of several Acts of Parliament,

An Account of Prohibited India Goods imported into the Warehouses in New Street, and Saint Helen, for Coast, Surat, and Private Trade Goods, in the Port of London, from Michaelmas 1798 to Michaelmas 1799, what delivered for Exportation during that Period, and what remained in the said Warehouses at Michaelmas 1799, as per Accounts: And also.

An Account of Prohibited East India Goods imported into the Bengal Warehouse in New,

Street, in the Port of London, from Michaelmas 1798 to Michaelmas 1799, also what exported during that Time, and what remained in the said Warehouse at Michaelmas 1799: And also,

An Account of Prohibited East India Goods remaining in His Majesty's Warehouse in the Port of London at Michaelmas 1798, what have been since brought in, as also what remained at Michaelmas 1799, and what exported: And also,

An Account of East India Goods, Prohibited to be worn in this Kingdom, in the respective Warehouses in the Out Ports, at Michaelmas 1798, what have been since brought in, what exported, as also what remained at Michaelmas 1799: And also,

An Account of Prohibited East India Goods, which remained out of the Bengal and Coast Warehouses, in Neiv Street, Bishopsgate Street, Private Trade Warehouses, and the Custom House in the Port of London, at Michaelmas 1798, in Order to be Dyed, Glazed, and Refreshed, what have been since delivered out, what returned, and what remained out at Michaelmas 1799:

And also, *

An Account of Naval Stores imported from Russia into the Port of London, from Michaelmas 1798 to Michaelmas 1799: And also,

An Account of Naval Stores imported from into the Ports of England, commonly called The Out Ports, from Michaelmas 1798 to Michaelmas 1799:

And also,

An Account of the Number of Ships which have been employed in the Whalfe Fishery to Davis's Streighis and the Greetdand Seas, distinguishing their Names,

Tonnage, Ports from whence they were fitted out, Ports where they were discharged, and also the Quantity of Blubber imported in each Ship in the Year 1799: And also,

A Lift of all Persons who were employed in the Service of the Customs, and have been put upon the Superannuation Fund since the ift December 1798, the Day on which the last Lift was submitted.

And then they withdrew.

And the Titles of the said Accounts and Lift were read.

Ordered, That the said Accounts and Lift do lie upon the Table, to be perused by the Members of the House.

The said Accounts and Lift are preserved amongst the other Papers of this Session.

Birley, and also the Road from Caldowell in the Parish of Bodenham, to a Place called Stretton's Bridge, in the Parish of Stretton Granfcm (over the River Froome) are very much out of Repair, narrow, and incommodious, and cannot be properly amended, improved, and kept in Voi.. 55.

The House, according to Order, proceeded to take into Consideration His Majesty's most Gracious Message of the 22d Day of January last: And also, the several Papers which were that Day presented to the House by Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer, by His Majesty's Command.

And the said Message was again read by Mr. Speaker.

And the said Papers were read.

A Motion was made, and the Question being proposed, That an humble Address be presented to His Majesty, to return His Majesty the Thanks of this House, for His most Gracious Message, and for having been graciously pleased to direct, that there should be laid before this House, Copies of the Communications recently received from the Enemy, and of the Answers which have been returned thereto by His Majesty's Command:

To allure His Majesty, that we consider the Conduct which His Majesty has held on this Occasion to be such as was dictated by His Regard to the moll important Interests of His Dominions, and that, while we join with His Majesty in looking eagerly to the Period when

265.

J 64.

it may become practicable to rc-establish the general Tranquillity of Europe on a sure and solid Foundation, and at the same Time provide effectually for the Security and permanent Prosperity of His People, we shall feel it in the Interval our indispenlible Duty to continue to His Majesty; on Behalf of those whom we represent, our firm and decided Support in such Measures as may bell tend to confirm the signal Advantages which have been obtained to the common Cause in the Course of the last Campaign, and to conduct the great Cornell in which His Majesty is engaged to a safe and honourable Conclusion; and that, imprefied with these Sentiments, we shall not fail to make such Provision as, under the present Circumstances, may appear to be necessary for the several Branches of the Public Service, and for the vigorous Prosecution of the War;

An Amendment was proposed to be made to the Question, by leaving out from the Words " His Majesty's Command," to the End of the Question.

And the Question being put. That the Words pro posed to be left out, Hand Part of the Question;

The House divided.

Resolved, That an humble Address be presented to His Majesty, to return His Majesty the Thanks of this House, for his moll Gracious Message, and for having been graciously pleased to direct, that there should be laid before this House, Copies of the Communications recently received from the Enemy, and of the Answers which have been returned thereto by His Majesty's Command:

To allure His Majesty, that we consider the ConduCk which His Majesty has held on this Occasion to be such as was didlated by His Regard to the moll important Interests of His Dominions, and that, while we join with His Majesty in looking eagerly to the Period when it may become practicable to re-establish the general Tranquillity of Europe on a sure and solid Foundation, and at the same Time provide effectually for the Security and permanent Prosperity of His People, we shall feel it in the Interval our indispenlible Duty to continue to His Majesty, on Behalf of those whom we represent, our firm and decided Support in such Measures as may bell tend to confirm the signal Advantages which have been obtained to the common Cause in the Course of the last Campaign, and to conduct the great Contest in which His Majesty is engaged to a safe and honourable Conclusion; and that, imprefied with these Sentiments, we shall not fail to make such Provision as, under the present Circumstances, may appear to be needfary for the several Branches of the Public Service, and for the vigorous Prosecution of the War.

Ordered, That the said Address be presented to His Majesty by such Members of this House as are of His Majesty's most honourable Privy Council.

Ordered, That His Majesty's said moll Gracious Message be taken into further Consideration this Day.

The subsequent Resolutions of the Committee, being severally read a Second Time, were postponed.

Ordered, That Leave be given to-bring in a Bill, pursuant to the First Resolution of the said Committee, and which has been agreed to by the House: And that Mr. Bragge, Mr. Rose, and Mr. Long, do prepare, and bring in, the fame.

Refo/ved, That this House will, upon Monday Morning next, resolve itself into a Committee of the whole House, to consider of the Acts mentioned in the subsequent Resolutions of the said Committee, and which have been postponed.

Ordered, That it be an Instruction to the Committee appointed to consider of Means for rendering more effectual the Provisions of an Act, made in the Thirteenth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, "An Act for better regulating the Assize and Making of Bread," that they do consider of the most effectual Means of remedying any Inconveniencies which may arise from the Deficiency of the last Crop of Grain.

Ordered, That the said Committee have Power to report their Proceedings, from Time to Time, to the House.

The Lord Hawke/bury reported to the House, That their Address of Yesterday (that His Majesty would be graciously pleased to give Directions, that the Account therein mentioned might be laid before this House) had been presented to His Majesty; and that His Majesty had commanded him to acquaint this House, that He will give Directions accordingly.

Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer presented to the House, according to Order, a Bill for further continuing an Act, made in the Thirty-eighth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, "An Act for empower- ing His Majesty, for a Time and to an Extent to be " limited, to accept the Services of such Parts of His " Militia Forces in this Kingdom as may voluntarily offer themselves to be employed in And the

feme was received; and read the First Time.

Resolved, That the Bill be read a Second Time.

Ordered, That the said Bill be read a Second Time upon Monday Morning next.

Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer presented to the House, according to Order, a Bill for further continuing an Act, made in the Thirty-seventh Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, "An Act for the " better Prevention and Punishment of Attempts to seduce Persons serving in His Majesty's Forces, by Sea or Land, from their Duty and Allegiance to His Majesty, or to incite them to Mutiny or Disobedience:" And the same was received j and read the First Time.

Resolved, That the Bill be read a Second Time.

Ordered, That the said Bill be read a Second Time upon Monday Morning next.

The House, according to Order, resolved itself into a Committee of the whole House, to consider of the Supply granted to His Majesty.

Mr. Speaker left the Chair.

Mr. Bragge took the Chair of the Committee.

Mr. Speaker resumed the Chair.

Mr. Bragge reported from the Committee, That they had come to several Resolutions; which they had directed him to report, when the House will please to receive the same.

Ordered, That the Report be received upon Monday Morning next.

Mr. Bragge also acquainted the House, That he was directed by the Committee to move, that they may have Leave to fit again.

Resolved, That this House will, upon Monday Morning next, resolve itself into a Committee of the whole House, to consider further of the Supply granted to His Majesty.

A PETITION of the distressed Debtors confined at Bodmin, in the County of And a!so,

A Petition of the Persons, whole Names are thereunto subscribed, being Prisoners confined for Debt in His Majesty's Gaol for the County of Salop . And also,

A Petition of the Debtors confined m His Majesty's Gaols for the County and the Town and County of the Town of Nottingham;

Were severally preferred to the House, and read } Complaining of their Distress, and praying Relief.

And the said Petitions were severally ordered to lie upon the Table.

Sir John Stuart reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the Provost, Magistrates, and Town Council, of the City of Aberdeen, was referred; That the Committee had examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Paving Bills, had been complied with; and that the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had dire died him to report the fame, as it appeared to them to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same Was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition a Member present informed your Committee, That the principal Avenues to the centrical Parts of the said City, from the South and North, by the Bridges of Dee and Dont are narrow, indirect, and incommodious; and the Increase of the Inhabitants of the said City, and Demand for Houses, and other Buildings, render it expedient to open certain new Streets in the several Lines of Direction mentioned in the Petition; which Improvements will be attended with great Utility and Advantage to the Public in general, and to the said City, and its Inhabitants in particular.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for opening and making Two new Streets in the City of Aberdeen: And that Sir John Stuart and Mr. Allardyct do prepare, and bring in, the fame.

Mr. Aftley presented to the House, according to Order, a Bill for dividing allotting and inclosing, the Commons and Waste Grounds, within the Parish of Langley, in the County of Norfolk: And the same was received} and read the First Time.

Resolved, That the Bill be read a Second Time.

Ordered, That the said Account do lie upon the Table, to be petufed by the Members of the House.

The House being informed that Mlv Porter (from the Commissioners of the Customs) attended at the Door, he was called in j and, at the Bar, presented to the House, pursuant to their Order,

An Account of the Total Amount of the Arrears due, on the 5th January 1800, from the Officers of the Customs in England, from the 5th January 1774 — lo far as the same can be made updistinguishing the Names of such Officers, and in what Situations they were or are employed, the Sums originally due from them, and when, and the Amounts and Dates of the Payments which have been made in Discharge thereof.

And then he withdrew.

And the Title of the said Account was read.

Ordered, That the said Account do lie upon the Table, to be perused by the Members of the House.

The said Account is preserved amongst the other Papers of this Session.

Mr. Wallace presented to the House, pursuant to their Address to His Majesty,

The Ordinary Estimate of His Majesty's Navy for Ordinary of the Year 1800: And also, Navy-

An Estimate of the Charge of what may be necef- Extra Nivy. lary for the Buildings, Re-buildings, and Repairs, of Ships of War, in His Majesty's and the Merchants Yards, and other Extra Works, over and above what areproposed to be done upon the Heads of Wear and Tear and Ordinary, for the Year 1800: And also.

An Estimate of the Monies which will probably be Transport wanted for the Service of the Transport Office, for the Service Year 1800.

Mr. Wallace also presented to the House, by His Majesty's Command,

Estimate of the probable Expence which maybe in- prisoners of curred for the Service of Sick Prisoners of War, in the War-present Year 1800.

And the Titles of the said Estimates were read.

The Ordinary Estimate of His Majesty's Navy is preservd amongst the other Papers of this Session; and the Abstract thereof, and the other Estimates, are as followed);

Mr. M'Dowall reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the Lord Provost, Magistrates, and Town Council of the City of , for them-

lelves, and on Behalf of the Community of the said City, was referred; That the Committee had examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Paving Bills, had not been complied with, as the Sentiments of the Three Incorporated Bodies of the City of Glasgow, respecting the Objects of the Petition,

could not be ascertained until the Election of the Magistrates had taken place, which was subsequent to the Quarter Sessions in October last, and 'which rendered it impracticable to give the Notices at the Times required by the Standing Orders of the House; and that the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House j and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, John Seton Carr, Esquire, being examined, said. That th'in habitants of the City of Glas have of 1 4® Years greatly increased in Number, and that would tend greatly to their Accommodation,' to that of other Persons referring to the said <fdty, that Footways and Pavements were made o«the Sides of the Streets thereof; that the said Street and Pavements were better lighted and clean fed; that the Police and Markets were better regulated; that a Superintendant of Police and Watchmen were appointed for the said City; that the said City were divided into Wards, and that Superintend-

His Majesty thinks it right to inform the House of Commons, that, in Consequence of Three Ships having arrived in the Ports of this Country from , on the Coast of Africa, with foul Bills of Health, which left that Place at the Time when the Plague raged there with the greatest Violence, and that Goods were put on Board the said Ships particularly susceptible of Infection, and under the most suspicious Circumstances, His Majesty has thought proper, by the Advice of His Privy Council, to order the said Ships and Cargoes to be destroyed, in Conformity to what has been the Usage in former Instances of the same Nature; and He recommends to the House of Commons, to consider whether any, and what, Allowance should be made to the Parties, for the Losses they may have sustained in Consequence of such Destruction of the Ships and Cargoes.

A Petition of William MDozcall, Esquire, being offered' to be presented to the House;

Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer (by His Majesty's Command) acquainted the House, That His Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House.

Then the said Petition was brought up, and read; Setting forth. That several Acts have been passed in the Reign of His present Majesty, for enabling His Majesty to direct the Issue ot Exchequer Bills, to a limited Amount, for the Aid and Accommodation of the Planters and Merchants connected with, and trading to, the Islands of Grenada and Saint Vincent, in Consideration of the heavy Losses that had been sustained in Consequence of the Insurredions which took place in these Islands; and that the Petitioner and James Andrew

Houfloun, and Robert HouJioun Rae, who are the Petitioners, Partners carrying on Trade under the Firm of Alexander HouJioun and Company, Merchants, in Glasgow, applied to the Commissioners acting under these Acts, and did obtain a Loan to the Amount of £.240,000, for the Re-payment of which the Petitioner and the said Partners, with certain Persons as Sureties for them, granted Security on Terms of the said Acts, to the Satisfaction of the Commissioners; and that this large Sum w'ould not have been issued by the Commissioners to the Petitioner and his Partners, unless they had proved the great Extent of their Funds, and the Embarrassfnents which the Partnership had sustained by the Public Calamities in the said Islands, as well as the Importance of supporting a Commercial House of such Magnitude, not for their own Sakes, but to prevent that extensive Ruin to others, which would have been the Consequence of withholding the Loan for which the Petitioners had applied: — The good Efleds of the Loan were soon felt, as the Petitioners were enabled thereby to pay very large Sums to their Creditors, and by that

County of the Town of So ;and to enable them to carry on so useful an Undertaking, they were authorized to raise and contribute, amongst themselves, any Sum not exceeding £. 56,000; but, in case the same should be found insufficient for completing the said Canal, they were authorized to raise any further Sum not exceeding £. 30,000, Fifteeen Thousand Pounds, Part thereof, by additional Shares, and the Residue at legal Interest, on the Credit of the said Canal, and the Tolls, Rates, and Duties thereof; and that the Petitioners have proceeded in the Execution of the said Act, and have laid out the Whole of the Line of the said Canal and Branch, and have cut a considerable Part thereof; but, from unforeseen Accidents and Expences, they have expended the Whole of the said Sum of £. 56,000, without having completed the said

Canal; and that the Petitioners have endeavoured to raise the further Sum of £. 15,000, by additional Shares, without Etfeft; but lire convinced they can procure the Whole of the said Sum of 30,000 by Mortgage of the Tolls, Rates, and Duties, of the said Canal, if they were empowered so to do; and that the Petitioners are apprehensive, that, from the great Advance of Materials and Labour, they shall have Occasion to borrow a further Sum of Money, over and above the said Sum of £. 30,000; and that the Petitioners find, in order to enable them effectually to complete and maintain the said Canal, it will be necessary that the said Act should be altered and amended: And therefore praying. That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for the Purposes aforesaid, under such Regulations and Restrictions, as the House shall think just and proper.

considerable Sum of Money hath been borrowed, and is now due and owing, and that the same cannot be paid off, nor the said District or Division of Road be maintained and kept in Repair, unless the Term of the said Acts be continued, and some of the Powers and Provisions thereof altered and amended, so far as relates to the said District or Division, and it is necessary that the Tolls to be collected thereon should be encreased: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill to continue the Term, and alter and enlarge the Powers, of the said Acts, so far as respects the said District or Division of Road, lying in the Counties of fV$ftptoreland and Lancaster, in such Manner, and under such Regulations, 'as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the fame, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

And it is referred to Mr. Lowther, Sir Michael Le Fleming, &c.: And they are to meet Tomorrow Morning, at Nine of the Clock, in the Speaker's Chamber; and have Power to fend for Persons, Papers, and Records.

Lord Viscount Stopford reported to the House, That their Address of Tuesday last (to return His Majesty the Thanks of this House for the gracious Communication contained in His Majesty's Message to this House, respecting the Ships and Cargoes which had arrived in the Ports of this Country from Mogadore, on the Coast of Africa, with foul Bills of Health) had been presented to His Majesty; and that His Majesty was pleased to receive the same most graciously.

Lord Viscount Stopford also reported to the House, That their Address of Tuesday last (that His Majesty would be graciously pleased to give Directions, that a List of the Names of the Persons now in Custody,- who have been committed in virtue of several Acts, made in the Thirty-eighth and Thirty-ninth Years of the Reign of His present Majesty, for empowering His Majesty to secure and detain such Persons as His Majesty shall suspect arc conspiring against His Person and Government j and of the Prisons in which they have been confined; together with the Dates of their Commitment, might be laid before this House) had been presented to His Majesty; and that His Majesty had commanded him to acquaint this House, that He will give Directions accordingly.

Lord Viscount likewise reported to the House,

That their Address of Yesterday (that His Majesty would be graciously pleased to give Directions, that a Copy of the Proceedings of the Lords of His Majesty's most Honourable Privy Council, respecting the Ships and Cargoes which had arrived in the Ports of this Country from Mogadore, on the Coast of Africa, with foul Bill of Health, and referred to in His Majesty's most Gracious Message of Tuesday last, might be laid before this House) had been presented to His Majesty; and that His Majesty had commanded him to acquaint this House, that He will give Directions accordingly.

Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer acquainted the House, That he had a Message from His Majesty to this House, signed by His Majesty; and he presented the same to the House; and it was read by Mr. Speaker (all the Members of the House being uncovered) and is as followeth; viz:

GEORGE R.

His Majesty is at present employed in concerting such Engagements with the Emperor of Germany, thie Elector of Bavaria, and other Powers of the Empire, as may

strengthen the Efforts of his Imperial Majesty, and materially conduce to the Advantage of the Common Cause in the Course of the ensuing Campaign; and His Majesty will give Directions that these Engagements, as soon as they shall have been completed and ratified, shall be laid before the House: But, in order to ensure the Benefit of this Co-operation at an early Period, His Majesty is desirous of authorizing His Minister to make provisionally such Advances as may be necessary, in the first Instance, for this Purpose; and His Majesty recommends it to the House to enable Him to make such Provision accordingly. G. R.

Ordered, That His Majesty's said raoft Gracious lyieflage be taken into Consideration Tomorrow Morning.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Mr. Samuel Churchill, Junior, being examined, said, That the

Roads leading from the Turnpike Road in through Ramsden, Charlbury, Enftone, and Great to the Turnpike Road on SwerfordHeath, in the County of Oxford, and from the Turnpike Road from -flock to Birmingham, at the Direction Poll to Charlbury, through Charlbury to the Turnpike Road from Chipping Norton to Burford, at a certain Place called Downs, in the said County of Oxford, are very much out of Repair, and in many Parts narrow and incommodious; and that it would be a great Convenience to the Neighbourhood, and of Public Utility, if the same were properly amended, widened, turned, altered, improved, and kept in Repair.

Thfc House being informed that one of the Sheriffs of the City of London attended at the Door, he was called in; and, at the Bar, presented to the House,

A Petition of the Lord Mayor, Aldermen, and Commons, of the City of London, in Common Council assembled.

And then he withdrew.

And the said Petition was read; Setting forth. That an Act waspaffed in the Thirty-fifth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for widening and improving the Entrance into the City of London near Temple , for making a more commodious Street or Passage at Snow

Hill, and for raising, on the Credit of the Orphans Fund, a Sum of Money for those Purposes ;and that another Act was passed, in the Thirty-eighth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, to explain, amend, and enlarge, the Powers of the before-mentioned Act , and that considerable Progress hath been made in the Execution of the Works directed by the said Two recited Acts, but it is found that the Money thereby authorized to be raised is insufficient to answer the several Purposes thereof; and that it is expedient the Land Tax charged on the Pre-mifies purchased, and to be purchased, for effecting the said Improvement, should be redeemed, and, in order to enable the Petitioners to effect such Redemption, and to fulfil the useful Intentions of the said Acts, it will be necessary that Power should be given them to raise a further Sum of Money, and that the Acts have been in some other Respects found defective, and require Explanation and Amendment: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill to amend, explain, and render more effectual, the said Two recited Acts, in such Manner, and under such Regulations, as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the fame, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

And it is referred to Mr. Alderman Curtis, The Lord Mayor of London,&c.: And they are to meet Tomorrow Morning, at Nine of the Clock, in the Speaker's Chamber; and have Power to lend for Persons, Papers, and Records.

Mr. Wallace presented to the House, according to Order, a Bill for the Regulation of His Majesty's Marine Forces while on Shore 2 And the same was received; and read the First Time.

Resolved, That the Bill be read a Second Time.

Ordered, That the said Bill be read a Second Time Tomorrow Morning.

Mr. Bragge presented to the House, according to Order, a Bill for punishing Mutiny and Desertion, and for the better Payment of the Army and their Quarters: And the same was received; and read the First Time.

Resolved, That the Bill be read a Second Time.

Mr. Speaker acquainted the House, That the Clerk had prepared, and laid upon the Table, a List of the Names of all the Members of thf House, who had delivered in Lifts in pursuance of the Directions of an Act,

passed in the Twenty-sixth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for the further Regulation of the Trial of Persons accul^d of certain Offences committed in the East Indies, and for other Purposes therein mentioned.

Ordered, That the Order of the Day, for the House to Committee resolve itself into a Committe of the whole House, to con- of SuPP y fider further of the Supply granted to His Majesty, be now read.

And the said Order being read accordingly;

The House resolved itself into the said Committee.

Mr. Speaker left the Chair.

Mr. Bragge took the Chair of the Committee.

Mr. Speaker resumed the Chair.

Mr. Bragge reported from the Committee, That they had come to a Resolution; which they had directed him to report, when the House will please to receive the same.

Ordered, That the Report be received Tomorrow Morning.

Hanber Navi- Mr. Henry Lascelles reported from the Committee, to gamm and whom the Petition of the Merchants, Underwriters, KiouPctiuon, Owners, and Mailers, of Ships of the Town of King ston-upon-HuU, and others, interested in the Shipping and Trade there, whose Hands are thereunto subscribed, was referred j That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To - prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Mr. Francis Wood, being examined, said, That the Navigation of the River Humber, from the said Port of Hull to the Sea, owing to the many Sands and Shoals therein, is difficult and dangerous, and, by the unskil-fulness of Persons who take upon them to pilot the Ships failing into and out of the said River, several Ships and Vessels, with their Crews and Cargoes, have been unfortunately wrecked and loll; that in bad Weather, Ships trading to and from the said Port, and such as take Shelter in the said River, are frequently obliged to leave their Anchors and Cables in the said River; and, when such Stores are found, the said Persons acting as Pilots, and others, finding the fame, either clandestinely deprive the Owners thereof, or demand and exact extravagant Sums of Money for, and as the Salvage thereof; and that, by reason of the Lighters carrying for Hire, Sand or Gravel for ballalling of Ships, and other Purposes, not being weighed and marked, the Ship Owners, and others, are, in general, imposed upon, by being obliged to pay for much less Weight or Quantity of Ballall, and other Articles, than the real and true Weight or Quantity thereof; that if such Persons as are thought proper for the Employment of River Pilots, were required to undergo an Examination in a formal and regular Manner, before some competent Body or Authority, as to their Abilities -and other Qualifications for such a Charge, and all others restrained from acting as Pilots in the said River, and were the Rates of Pilotage specified and limited, the Government of Pilots, the Adjustment of Salvage, and the Regulation of Ballad Lighters, veiled in certain Commissioners, the same would be a Means of preserving many Lives and much Property, and of preventing the Frauds and Impositions above-mentioned, and would also be of general Utility to the Trade and Shipping of the said Port of Vot. 53.

Mr. Anthony Somerfcales and Mr. Charles Allison confirmed the above Evidence.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for the Appointment and Regulation of Pilots for the conducting of Ships and Vessels into and out of the Port of Kingston upon-Hull; and for ascertaining the Salvage for Anchors, Cables, and other Ships' Materials, found in the River Humber; and for the better ascertaining the Tonnage of Ballad Lighters employed at the said Port:

And that Mr. Henry Lascelles, Mr. , and

Mr. Samuel Thornton, do prepare, and bring in> the fame.

A Message from the Lords, by Mr. Leeds and Mr.

Pefys:

Mr. Speaker,

The Lords have commanded us to Acquaint this House, That the Lords have come to the following Resolution and Agreement; viz>

Resolved, By the Lords Spiritual and Temporal, in Parliament assembled. That, in consequence of the high Price and deficient Supply of Wheat and other Grain, it is expedient to adopt such Measures as may be practicable for diminishing the Consumption thereof; during the Continuance of the present Pressure, and for introducing the Use of such Articles as may conye niently be substituted in the Place thereof.

AGREEMENT.

In consequence of the high Price of Grain, and the Evils arising therefrom. We, the undesigned, agree, That, until the Tenth Day of October next, we will, not consume, nor permit to be consumed, in any Week, within our respective Families, m«t Wheaten Bread than in the Proportion of One Quartern Loaf foreaCh of the Individuals of whom our laid Families may be composed; and also, that, during the said Period, we will discontinue, and cause to be difcaotinued, within., our said Families, all Pastry.

And then the Messengers withdrew.

Ordered, That the said Resolution and Agreement be referred to the Consideration of the Committee of1 the whole House, to whom it is referred to (ofifider further of the Report, which was made from the Corn mittee appointed to consider of Means for rendering more effectual the Provisions of an Act, made in the Thirteenth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, "An Act for better regulating the Assize and making of Bread j" and who were mstructed to consider of the most effectual Means of remedying any Inconveniences which may arise from the Deficiency of the last Crop of Grain.

of all the Principal Money and Interest which shall be then due and owing to the said Governor and ! Company upon all such Tallies, Exchequer Or-

That, in Consideration of the above proposed ' Extension of their Charter for Twenty-one Years, ' -and a Grant of their other Privileges, Employments, Advantages, and Immunities above-mentioned, the said Governor and Company are wil-

ling to advance the Sum of Three Millions Sterling for the Public Service, to be paid on such ! Days during the present Year, and in such Manner, as Parliament shall direct and appoint, the Re-payment thereof to be secured by Exchequer Bills, to be made out at the Time of such Advance, by virtue of an Act to be passed in this Session of Parliament, and to be made payable at the Expiration of Six Years from the Date thereof, without Interest, the said Exchequer Bills to be charged and chargeable upon the first Aids or Supplies which shall be granted by Parliament, for the Service of the Year One thousand Eight hundred and Six; and, in case sufficient Aids or Supplies should not be granted by Parliament for that Purpose, before the Fifth Day of April One thou-- \ - land Eight hundred and Six, the same to be charged and chargeable upon, and to be repaid out of, the Consolidated Fund.

Provided, that the said Governor and Company shall have the Option of being repaid the said Sum of Three Millions at any Time before the Expiration of the said Term of Six Years, in case the ‘Price of the-Three per Centum Consolidated Annuities shall be Eighty per Centum, or more, upon giving Sir Months Notice for that Purpose to the Lords Commissioners of His Majesty'sTreasury; and upon such Re-payment, the said Governor and Com-.. pany shall deduct or allow a Discount to the Public, at and after the Rate of Five Pounds per Centum per Annum, on the Sum repaid for such Part of the said ' Term of Six Years as shall then remain unexpired. A Petition of His Majesty's most loyal and dutiful Subjects, the Lord Mayor, Aldermen, and Liverymen, of the City of London, at the Guildhall of the said City, the 19th Day of February 1800, in Common Hall assembled, was presented to the House, and read; Seting forth. That the Petitioners deeply lament the Calamities inseparable from a State of War, but more particularly those which have resulted from the present Conflict, because they conceive it to have been more indefinite in its Objcift, and devastating in its Progress, than any War this Country has hitherto been engaged in } and that the Petitioners deprecate Wars undertaken

.cither for the secret or avowed Purpose of imposing a *

Government on another County, or in any Manner interfering in its internal Concerns; and that, impressed with these Considerations, they have not in any Instance sanctioned or approved of the present War, but, on the contrary, have, by Instructions to their Representatives in Parliament, by Petitions addressed to His Majesty, and to the House, endeavoured to stop that Effusion of human Blood with which Europe has so long been deluged; and that, in their Petition presented to the House so far back as the 26th of January 1795, among other Things, they stated it as their Opinion, that none of the Ends proposed by the present War had been or appeared likely to be obtained; and that in their said Petition they further declared it to be their decided Conviction, from their View of Public Measures, that the Principle upon which the War appeared then to be carried on neither was, nor could be, essential to the Prof-perity, the Liberty, or the Glory of the Empire;

and humbly praying, That the House, declaiming all Right of interfering in the internal Concerns of France, would, be pleased to take such Measures as they in their' Wisdom should think proper, for the Purpose of promoting a speedy Peace between Great Britain and the Powers with whom we are now at War j and that, to the inexpressible Concern and Disappointment of the Petitioners, the War was unfortunately perlilted in, and more than Five Years have elapsed since that Period, during which Time the Fears and Apprehensions which they then expressed to the House have not only been realized but greatly exceeded, a Series of the moil melancholy Events and unexampled Misfortunes have ensued j the Petitioners forbear detailing the long and bloody Catalogue of Disasters which have attended the War, with the various expensive and destru<ftive Expeditions we have been engaged in, which have produced the most lerious Effects upon the Commerce and Manufactories of the Country; the Petitioners will not enumerate the long Train of aillidting Events attending the late unhappy Rebellion in Ireland, and the present distracted and unsettled State of that Country; neither will they dwell upon the exorbitant Price of Provisions, which bears so hard upon the middle and poorer Cialfes of the People, already borne down with an intolerable Pressure of Taxation, all which Circumstances lepa-rately, and combinedly, powerfully solicit the Return of Peace; and that, in this alarming Situation of Public Affairs, it is with the deeped Regret they have observed the Overtures of the French Contul, for terminatin'; Hof-

..... . O

till tics, rejected by His Majesty's Councils, and a Design more openly avowed than at any former Period of prole-cuting the War for the Purpose of restoring to the Government of France the ancient Line of the Bourbon Family; the Petitioners are the more astonished at such a Proceeding, because they did not conceive it possible that, after a bitter and unavailing Conflict of Seven Years, after a Sacrifice of so many Thousands of Lives, and lb many Millions of Money, His Majesty's Ministers could want the Result of Experience, and the Evidence of Facts, to demonstrate to them the Impracticability of a Project lb utterly incompatible with the true Interests of these Kingdoms; the Petitioners cannot sufficiently impress upon the House the Impolicy of perfe-vering in a Contest which, even if it were to prove fuc-. celsful, appears to be principally calculated for the Aggrandizement of our Aiiies, who have nevertheless, on different Occasions, shewn no Reluctance to conclude a Peace, and whole Exertions, even in their own Cause, can only be procured by the lavish Expenditure of this devoted Country; and, conceiving that no adequate Advantage can arise from a further Prosecution of Hostilities, and that the present Period is highly favourable to Negociation, the Petitioners pray, that the House will take such Measures as they in their \Vifdom may think proper, towards promoting an immediate Negociation with the Government of France, for the Purpose of restoring to His Majesty's Subjects the Blessings of Peace,

That an Act was pafifed, in the Twelfth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for embanking, draining, and preserving, certain Fen Lands and Low Grounds in the Parish of Ramsey, in the County of Huntingdon, and in the Parishes of Doddington, March,

and Chatteris, within the Isle of Ely, in the County of Cambridge, and for amending the Road from a certain Bridge, in the Parish of Chatteris aforesaid, called. Carter's Bridge, by a Drain called Vermnydens, or The Forty Feet Drain, to a Bridge called The Forty Feet Bridge, in the said Parish of Ramsey, and that, by the said Act, the said Lands and Grounds are divided into Two separate Districts, or Divisions, with rel'ped to the repairing and keeping in Repair the several Outward Banks therein particularly described, and are therein called by the Names of The Upper D or Division, and The loiter DislriEl or Division, and separate Commissioners are appointed for embanking the said Upper District or Division, with Power to alfefs and rate all the Lands and Grounds being Private Property within that District, except such as in the said Act are excepted, in any Yearly Sums of Money, not exceeding in any one Year, except in the First Year after the passing of the said Act, One Shilling per Acre, to defray the Expence of embanking; and that the said Commissioners have proceeded in the Execution of the Powers vested in them, and have caused the Banks of the said Upper District to be repaired from Time to Time at a considerable Expence, and that the Money, authorized to be raised as aforesaid, hath been found insufficient to defray the Expence of repairing and keeping in Repair the said Banks, and on that Account the Commissioners have borrowed a considerable Sum of Money on the Credit of the said Rates and Taxes, which still remains due; and that the said Banks are become of late greatly decayed, and it is necessary that an additional Tax should be laid on the said Fen Lands and Low Grounds, to enable the Commissioners to repair the said Banks, and pay off the Money

That the said Standing Order of the House, of the 27th Day of June, in the last Session of Parliament; relative to Bills of Inclosure, be repealed.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, in all Bills oflnclosure, there be inserted a Clause compelling the Commissioners to keep, at the Office of their Clerk, a Book of Accounts, open at all reasonable Times, during the Progress of the Inclosure, and till the Accounts are finally settled, for the Inspection of any of the Proprietors; which Book shall contain an Entry of the Particulars of all Sums of Money raised or expended by virtue of any Powers granted by the Act, under a Penalty on such Commissioners, or their Clerk, for neglecting or refuting the fame: — And also, a Clause, providing, that all Monies to be raised under and by virtue of the Powers contained in such Act, shall, as often as the same thall amount to the Sum of £. 50. be paid into the Hands of some Banker, or of such other Person or Persons as shall be approved by a Majority in Value of such Proprietors, who shall be present at the First Meeting of the said Commissioners, and in the Notice of which Meeting shall be expressed the Intention of then appointing such Banker, or such other Person or Persons j and that no Monies be issued out of the Hands of such Banker, or other Person or Persons, without an Order of the Commissioners, specifying the Person to whom the same are payable, and the Service for which the same are due; and that the Balance (if any) upon the final Settlement of Accounts, shall be immediately repaid to the Land Owners, in Proportion (o the Sums respectively paid by them: — And also, a Clause, providing, that the Award shall be read and executed by the Commissioners in the Presence of the Proprietors who may attend at a Special General Meeting called for that Purpose, of which Ten Days Notice at least shall be given in some Newspaper, tobe named, circulating within the County; which Execution of such Award shall be proclaimed the next Sunday in the Pari ft) Church; from the Time of which Proclamation only, and not before, such Award shall be considered as complete.

Ordered, That the said Report be taken into further Consideration upon Monday Morning next.

lVtitian of Li- A Petition of His Majesty's most. loyal and dutiful London 0t 3ubjefts, the there-undersigned Liverymen of the City of London, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners deeply lament the Calamities inseparable from a State of War, more particularly those which have arisen from the present Conflict, seeing not only the Honour, but the very Existence of all that is dear to a Nation, depends upon its successful Termination} and that at a Common Hall of the Livery of London, assembled on the 19th Instant, a Petition was voted to the House, containing Sentiments not founded in Fast, and consequently repugnant to the Feelings of the Petitioners, for which Reason they have dissented, and do dissent, therefrom; for thpy deny that a Scries of the most melancholy Events and unexampled Misfortunes have attended His Majesty's Arms} on the contrary, surrounding Nations bear Testimony to the Zeal and Bravery of His Majesty's Troops, and the World looks with Astonishment and Admiration on the Success which has every where attended the British Navy; nor can the Petitioners attribute to the War the Scarcity arising from an uncommonly bad Season; nor is it possible for them to admit as a Fad the Assertion, that destructive Expeditions have produced the most serious Effects upon the Commerce and Manufactories of the Country, as they well know both to be in a most flourishing Situation; and that, anxioully delirous as the Petitioners must be for the Return of Tranquillity, yet it is a Duty which they most readily follow, to submit to the Wisdom of the House and His Majesty's Executive Government the Measures, the Time, and the Means, for procuring to the Nation a just and permanent Peace} for all which the Petitioners most humbly pray.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

Care, and Protection, of the Petitioners; and that such Removal would not only be a Violation of the ancient Rights and Privileges of the Petitioners, but also be productive of themost ruinous and distressing Consequences to divers Incorporated Societies and Companies, as well as to great. Numbers of Individuals, acting under the Authority of the Petitioners, and employed in carrying on the said Trade and Commerce; and that the said Bill proposes to lay a further and general Impost upon the whole Commercial Tonnage which enters the Port of London, excepting Coasting Vessels; and that, the Petitioners and their Predecessors, ever anxious to accommodate, promote, and increasetheTrade of the Port of Louden, have from Time to Time devised and offered to execute Plans conducive to that End, and, actuated by such Motives, the Petitioners did, in Conjunction with the India Planters and Merchants, apply for and obtain, during the last Session of Parliament, an Act for rendering more commodious, and for better regulating, the Port of London; and that the said Act provides against the Perils and Delays attending the Navigation of the River, by a Navigable Cut, or Cannl, across the ljle of Dogs-, and that it provides for the Reception and complete Accommodation, in Docks, of the Whole of the West India Trade; and that it authorizes the Appointment of Harbour Mailers, and gives full Powers for effectually regulating the mooring and Rationing of the

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, a Member present informed Your Committee,-That there are within the several Parishes, Townships, or Places, above-mentioned, certain large Tracts of Low Lands, the Property of the Petitioners and others, containing in the Whole Ten Thousand Acres, and upwards, through which the Rivers Derwent and Harford have their separate and conjoined Courles: That the Channels and Beds of the said Rivers are very insufficient to contain and convey the Flood Waters thereof within their present Limits; and such Flood Waters being also greatly impeded in their Passage by the many winding Directions in which the said Rivers take their Courses, the said Lands are thereby subject to be frequently overflowed and injured, and by reason thereof the same are incapable of any considerable Improvement, or of being put into a State of Cultivation; and that in order to prevent such Injury to the said Lands, and to improve the same by an effectual Drainage, it is expedient that a Cut, of sufficient Dimensions to afford a free Passage for the Waters of the Derwent in all Times of Flood, should be made, to branch out of the same River at or near a Place within the Parish of Hack-ness, in the said North Riding, called Ever ley, and to be continued from thence Eastwards, through certain Lands within the same Parish, to and into a Brook within the Parish of Scalby, within the same Riding, called Seal by Beck, and the same Cut to be from thence continued in or near to the present Course of the said BrOok, through the said Parish of Scalby, down to the Sea, there to discharge the Whole of such Waters: That the Beds or Channels of the said Rivers iliould be so deepened, widened, altered, and embanked, where necessary, as at all Times to' admit, within the proper Limits thereof, a free Course for the Waters having to pals along the fame; and that such Drainage as aforesaid vviil be highly beneficial to the Petitioners, and of Public Utility.

A Petition of the Curate of the perpetual Curacy Of Walls-End, and of the Chapel Wardens, Land Owners, and Inhabitants, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, on Behalf of themselves, and the several other Persons, Land Owners, and Inhabitants of, and in the Parish of Walls -End, and County of Northumberland, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. Committee on Ordered, That the Order of the Day, for the House to National Debt ref0|vc into a Committee of the whole House,

upon the Bill for granting to His Majesty the Sum of Two Hundred Thousand Pounds, to be issued and paid to the Governor and Company of the Bank of England, to be by them placed to the Account of the Commissioners for the Reduction of the National Debt, be now read.

And the said Order being read accordingly;

The House resolved itself into the said Committee.

Mr. Speaker left the Chair.

Mr. Long took the Chair of the Committee.

Mr. Speaker resumed the Chair.

Mr. Long reported from the Committee, That they had gone through the Bill, and made several Amendments thereunto; which they had directed him to report, when the House will please to receive the same.

Ordered, That the Report be received Tomorrow Morning.

Mr. Baker reported from the Committee, That they1 had come to several Resolutions; which they had directed him to report, and had also directed him to make several Motions, when the House will please to receive the same.

Ordered, That the Report be now received.

Mr. Baker accordingly reported from the said Commit- reported, tee the Resolutions which the Committee had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place j and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same were read; and are as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That, whenever the Average Prices of Wheat, and fine Wheaten Flour, ascertained and published in The London Gazette, under the Authority of any Act or Acts of Parliament, shall be less than Ninety Shillings per Quarter of Wheat, or Sack of Wheaten Flour, respectively, there shall be given, on every Quarter of Wheat, and on every Barrel of fine Wheaten Flour, which shall be imported into Great Britain, from any Port of Europe, South of Cape Finefterre, or. from any Port in the Mediterranean,

or in Africa, or from any of His Majesty's Colonies in America, or The United States, before the 1 ft Day of October 1800, a Bounty equal to the Difference between such Average Prices in The London Gazette, and Ninety Shillings per Quarter of Wheat, or Barrel of Flour, respectively.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That, whenever the current Price of Rice imported into this Kingdom, to be ascertained by the Prices in the London Market, shall be left than One Pound and Fifteen Shillings per Hundred Weight, there shall be given, on every One Hundred Weight of Rice imported into ' >

Great Britain before the ift Day of October 1800, a Bounty equal to the Difference between such Average Price and One Pound Fifteen Shillings.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That the Duties now payable oh Swedish Herrings, dried or cured, imported into this Kingdom, do cease and determine.

Mr. Baker also reported from the said Committee,

That he was directed by the Committee to move the House, that Leave be given to bring in a Bill to encourage the Cultivation of Pota»oes on Waste Lands, for a Time to be limited: And also,

That Leave be given to bring in a Bill to explain and amend an Act, made in the Thirty-sixth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, "An Act " for the better Regulation of MillsAnd allb,

That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for better regulating the Price and Assize of Bread: And also.

That Leave be given to bring in a Bill to prohibit, for a Time to be limited, the Use of Wheat in making Starch.

Ordered, That the said Report be taken into further Consideration Tomorrow Morning.

Ordered, That such a Number of Copies of the said Report be printed, as shall be sufficient for the Use of the Members of the House.

in the Parish of Whitwick, in the County of Leicester, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That there are, within the said Lordship or Liberties, several Open Fields, Meadows, Pastures, Commons, and Waste Grounds, which lie intermixed in small Parcels, and are, in their present Situation, incapable of Improvement, and it would greatly tend to the Advantage of the several Persons interested therein, to have the same divided and inclosed, and specific Parts thereof allotted and awarded to each Proprietor, according to his or her Interest therein j and that certain Allotments, or Divisions of Land, within- the said Lordship or Liberty of Thringstone, have heretofore been made amongst the Proprietors, by private Agreement, which would be of great Advantage and Benefit to the said Proprietors to be confirmed: And therefore praying. That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for dividing and inclosing the said Open Fields, Meadows, and Commons, and for confirming the said Allotments and Divisions, in such Manner as to the House shall seem meet.

A Petition of the Right honourable Thomas James Lord Bulkeley, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That, between the Isle of and the Isle of Anglesea, in the Irifi Channel, at a Place called Penmon, on the-Coast of Anglesea, are certain dangerous Rocks, on which many Ships and Vessels have been wrecked for want of a Lighthouse on the said Isle of Priejlholme, which would direct the Navigator, when embayed on that Coast, to shoot the Gut, or Sound, which separates the said Isle of Pries holme from the said Isle of Anglesea, and thereby gain the safe and commodious Harbour of Beaumaris; and that the Petitioner is seised in Fee of the said Isle of Pries holme, and is willing to erect and maintain a good and sufficient Lighthouse thereon, and to cause the same to be properly lighted at all necessary Times, at his own Costs and Charges, upon Condition of being allowed such Indemnification byWay of Tonnage Rates on Shipping, as may be just and reasonable { and that the Petitioner has had the Sandtion of the Lords Commissioners of the Admiralty, and the Corporation of Trinity House, and the Reports from the said Boards have been transmitted to the Guild of Merchants at Liverpool, for their Approbation: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for the Purposes aforesaid, under such Rules, Orders, and Regulations, as to the House shall seem meet.

the Messuages, Lands, Tenements, and Hereditaments, situate within the said Three Parishes of All Saints, Saint Peter, and Saint Mary, in Maldon aforesaid, with Payment thereof within Ten Years from the passing of an Act for that Purpose, to be charged, raised, and levied on such Messuages, Lands, Tenements, and Hereditaments, by an equal Rate or Assessment, in Proportion to the Value of such Estates respectively; and that there is a great Thoroughfare over the said Bridge for all Manner of Car- - , riages, the same being situate in a Public Road, and there will be great Danger of its giving way when any Carriage heavy laden passes over, or if a Barge in passing under Should strike against it, whereby many Lives may be loft, and great Injury sustained, and it therefore is become absolutely necessary, for the Safety of the Public in general, that a new Bridge should be immediately erected, which Necessity did not arise until after the Time limited by the House for giving the Notices required by the Standing Orders relative to Bills for building Bridges: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for re-building the said Bridge, and that the Money necessary for that Purpose may be raised, levied, and repaid, by such Ways and Means as to the House shall seem meet, and that the Petitioners may be permitted forthwith to give the Notices required by the Standing Orders.

That they may be heard, by their Counsel, against the said Bill, and that the same may not pass into a Law.

A Motion was made, and the Question being proposed, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of the Committee to whom the said Bill is committed; and that the Petitioners be heard, by their Counsel, before the said Committee, upon their Petition, if they think fit;

An Amendment was proposed to be made to the Question, by leaving out from the Word (committed,) to the End of the Question.

And the Question being put, That the Words proposed to be left out, stand Part of the Question;

It passed in the Negative.

Then the main Question, so amended, being put;

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of the Committee, to whom the said Bill is committed.

A Petition of the Trustees of the British Mifeum, being offered to be presented to the House;

Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer (by; His Majesty's Command) acquainted the House, That His Majesty, having been intormed of the Contents of the said Pe-tion, recommends it to the Consideration of the House.

Then the said Petition was brought up, and read; Setting forth, That in the Second Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, the said Trustees represented to Parliament that the Sum allowed them for the Establishment and Support of the said Museum, was reduced to a Capital of £. 30,000, Reduced Bank Annuities, the Dividend of which, amounting to £. 900, was, notwithstanding their utmost Attention to the forming their Establishment with Frugality, greatly insufficient for that Purpose; upon which Representation they have, at sundry Times, obtained from the House various Sums, to supply the Deficiency of their Income, which Sums, together with the Salary allotted t<o the King's Librarian, Yearly amounting to about £. 250, have proved insufficient to defray the necessary Expences of the said Museum, and what now remains in the Hands of the Trustees is not sufficient to carry on the Purposes of the Trust, without the Aid of Parliament: And therefore praying the House to grant them such further Support, towards enabling them to carry on the Execution of the Trust reposed in them by Parliament, for the general Benefit of Learning and useful Knowledge, as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

That the Petitioner is Lessee under the Crown, for a Term of which about Thirteen Years are unexpired, of all the Chains for mooring Vessels in the River Thames between London Bridge and Bugby's Hole, with full Right of placing as many Chains, from Time to Time, as the N umber of Ships or other Circumstances may require, and is desirous, at his own Expence, to carry into Effect a Plan for the Improvement of the Mooring Chains, by which his Estate will be very largely benefited j and in so doing he doubts not but he shall, in a great Degree, afford the Means of putting an End to the Inconvenience now felt, which arises from the crowded State of the Shipping, and the Obstruction thereby occasioned to the Navigation of the River; which Inconvenience, if the above Plan is carried into Effect, may be remedied in the Space of Two Years; and that if the Bill now depending in the House, for making Wet Docks, Basons, Cuts, and other Works, for the greater Accommodation and Security of Shipping, Commerce, and Revenue, within the Port of London, should pass into a Law as it now Hands, the Petitioner's Estate, under the Lease above mentioned, which is now of great Value, will be totally or very nearly annihilated, as the Object of the Bill is to take the greatest Part of the Ships out of the River into Docks

State, at length became impassable, and in Consequence thereof, such Parts which remained were, in the Month, of June 1795, pulled down, whereby great Inconvenience has arisen to the Public, as there has been no convenient Passage over the Thames in that Part of the Country ever since; and that the Petitioners are informed, it is intended to erect a new Bridge over the Thames, in a Situation more convenient and useful for the Public; viz. from a Place called Neville's Bridge, in the Parish of New Windsor, to the opposite Shore near a Place called Southby, in the Panih of Datchet aforesaid, which is at some Distance from the Scite of the former Bridge; and that the said new Bridge will form a Communication between the T«nvns, Parishes, and Places above mentioned, and divers other Parts of the Kingdom: — And, he further said. That it would be a great Benefit and Convenience to the Petitioners, ami others. Inhabitants of the said Towns, Paiiihes, and Places, by making a shorter Communication between the Metropolis, and the said Town of New and be of Public Utility, if a Road were made from the said Town of New Windsor over the said intended Bridge, and from thence to or near Datchet Common Gate, on the Road from Datchet to Stan well, in the County of Middlesex, and if the Road from thence to the Hand Pod at Boyle, were amended, widened, and kept in Repair; and if a new Road were made Irom the said Hand Pod to or near the Sixteenth Mile Stone on the Road from Colnbrook to London, orlomc other convenient Spot on the said lad mentioned Road.

Ordered, That the said Report do lie upon the Table.

Mr. Wallace, according to Order, reported from the Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred to consider of giving further Encouragement to the Importation of Corn and Flour, the Resolutions which the Committee had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same were read j and are as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,. That, whenever the Average Price of Wheat, ascertained and published in The London Gazette, under the Authority of any Act or Acts of Parliament, shall be less than Eighty-five Shillings per Quarter, there shall be given, on every Quarter of Wheat which shall be imported into Great Britain, from any of the Ports of the Baltic, or from any of the Ports of Germany, or any Ports North of the Texet, before the ill: Day of October 1800, a Bounty equal to the Difference between such Average Price in The London Gazette and Eighty-five Shillings/w Quarter of Wheat.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, whenever the Average Price of Wheat, ascertained and published in The London Gazette, under the Authority of any Act or Acts of Parliament, shall be less than Ninety Shillings per Quarter, there shall be given, on every Quarter of Wheat which shall be imported into Great Britain, from the Port of Archangel, before the ill Day of October 1800, a Bounty equal to the Difference between such Average Price in The London Gazette and Ninety Shillings per Quarter of Wheat.

The said Resolutions, being severally read a Second Time, were, upon the Question severally put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

Ordered, That it be an Instruction to the Committee of the whole House, to whom the Bill for granting Bounties on the Importation of Wheat, Wheaten Flour, and Rice, for a Time to be limited, is re-committed, that they have Power to make Provision in the said Bill, pursuant to the said Resolutions.
