That in putting the said Act in Execution, the Petitioners find it will be necessary to take down a considerable Number of Houses situate in the said Parish, which are subject to the Payment of the Rates collected under the Authority of the said several Acts, and the Ground whereon the same Hand will be used for the Purposes of the Dock and Improvements intended to be eftefted by the said Bill; and that the taking down of the said Houses will occasion a considerable Diminution in the Produce of the Rate to be collected under the Acts, and the Burthen will be consequently increased on the other Inhabitants of the said Parish: And therefore praying, That Provision may be made in the said Bill for indemnifying the Petitioners for the Injury they may sustain in Manner aforesaid, or that the Petitioners may have such other Relief in the Premises as to the House shall l'eem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table, until the Report which was made from the Committee, to whom the said Bill was committed, be taken into further Consideration.

A Petition of the several Persons, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, being Owners or Occupiers of Estates within the Parish of Iver, in the County of Buckingham, was presented to the House, and read; Taking Notice of the Bill for dividing, allotting, and incIdling, the Open Common Fields, Lammas Lands, Commons, Heaths, Moors, and Waste Lands, within the Parish of Iver, in the County of Buckingham; and Setting forth,

That, if the said Bill should pals into a Law as it now Rands, the Petitioners conceive their Rights and Inte-relts will lie very materially injured: And therefore praying, That they may be heard by themselves, or Counsel, agauilt such Parts of the said Bill as affect their Rights and Interests, and that they may have such Relief in the Premises as to the House shall l'eem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of the Committee, to whom the said Bill is committed; and that the Petitioners be heard, by themselves, or Counicl, before the said Committee, upon their Petition, if they think fit.

Ordered, That it be an Instruction to the fit id Committee, that they do admit Counsel to be heard, at the same Time, in Favour of the said Bill, against the said Petition.

Ordered, That all have Voices who come to the Committee to whom the said Bill is committed.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Mr. Thomas William Tottie, being examined, said, That there

are within the said Township certain Commons and Waste Lands, which are capable of much Improvement by Drainage and Inclosure, but, in their present uncultivated State, are of little Value: and that it would be a great Advantage if the same were drained and inclosed, and an additional Benefit to the Proprietors of Estates, within the said Township, if their Estates were exonerated from Tythes, and full Compensation made for the fame, and also, if proper Powers were given to drain and improve such Estates: That there are within the said Township certain Embankments, which would be of much greater Utility if the same were raised and repaired, and Provisions for upholding them in future.

My Lords and Gentlemen,

It is with the greatest Satisfaction that I receive, from My Two Houses of Parliament, this dutiful and loyal Address, expressing their Concurrence in those Resolutions which have been proposed by the Lords and Commons of Ireland, as the Articles of a Legislative Union between My Two Kingdoms. I shall, without Delay, communicate to My Parliament of Ireland the Sentiments and the Declarations contained in this Address; and the Dispositions which have been manifested by My Parliaments in both Kingdoms, afford Me the best Pledge of the speedy and prosperous Conclusion of this great Measure: An Event to which I look forward with the most anxious Expectation, as tending, above all others, to secure and perpetrate the Happiness of all My Subjects.

Mr. William Henry Bouverie accordingly reported from the said Committee, That the Committee had examined the Matters of the said Petitions, which they had directed to be reported to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as folio wet h; viz.

T<f prove the Allegations of the first mentioned Petition, Mr. John Hodding, Town Clerk of the City of New Sarum, being examined, said, That the said City and the Close thereof exercise an exempt Jurisdiction from the said County, and had an ancient Gaol within the same, for the Confinement of Felons, Debtors, and other Prisoners of the said City, and of the Close thereof ;. and that the said Gaol was by the Authority of Parliament, a few Years since, taken down, and another was intended to be erected in its Stead; but it being considered as more eligible that the said Prisoners mould in future be confined in the County Gaol of Fisherton Anger, adjoining to the said City, which is large and Commodious, the Magistrates for the said City have offered a Compensation, and have entered into an Agreement with the Magistrates of the said, County, which has been approved and confirmed at the Four last several Quarter Sessions of the Peace for the said County, for giving to the said exempt Jurisdiction a Power of confining in the said County Gaol, Felons, Debtors, and other "Prisoners, from the said exempt Jurisdiction.

To prove the Allegations of the second mentioned Petition, an Act, passed in the Twenty-fifth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for removing and re-building the Council Chamber, Guildhall, and Gaol, of the said City, and for ascertaining the Tolls of the Market, and regulating the Chairmen within the said City, was read; by which it appeared. That the Mayor and Commonalty of the said City were thereby authorized to build and maintain within the said City, or the Suburbs or Precincts thereof, aGaol for the said City and the Close thereof, and to take upon themselves the Custody and Safe-keeping of such Persons as should be confined therein; and it was by the said Act provided, that until such new Gaol should be erected, all the Debtors, Felons, and other Persons, within the said Cky and Close thereof, who then were or should be liable or ought to be committed to the said Common Gaol of the said City, should, as Occasion should require, be committed by the Justices of the Peace for the said City, or Close thereof, to, and should be confined in, the Common Gaol of the County of Hilts: And,

Mr. John Hodding, being again examined, said, That the old Gaol belonging to the said City was, under the Authority of the said Act, taken down, and a new one was intended to be erected, but it hath not been done, it being conceived that such Debtors, Felons, and other Persons, would be more safely and conveniently confined in the said County Gaol, the same being very large and secure, and immediately adjoining to the said City, than they woold be in a new Gaol to be erected within the said City or the Suburbs or Precincts thereof, as directed 3

by the said Act, and as stated in the said Petition already presented to the House; and it is therefore expedient that, instead of erecting a new Gaol, pursuant to the Directions of the said Act, the Agreement entered into by the Petitioners with the Magistrates for the said County, should be ratified and carried into Effect, and it is necessary that some of the Powers and Provisions Of the said Act should be explained, amended, and enlarged: That Doubts having arisen respecting the Office of Clerk of the said City, and the Rights, Privileges, and Appurtenances thereunto belonging, veiled in and by the said Act in the Mayor and Commonalty of the said City, an Agreement had been entered into with the Right Reverend Father in God John Lord Bishop of Sarum, to whom the Gift or Grant of the said Office belonged, before the passing of the said Act, for an Explanation of so much thereof as relates to the Grant of such Office, and the Rights and Privileges of the fame.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for repealing so much of an Act, passed in the Twenty-fifth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled,

" An Act for the Removal and Re-building the Council " Chamber, Guildhall, and Gaol of the City of New " Sarum, and for ascertaining the Tolls of the Market, u and regulating the Chairmen, within the said City," as requires the Mayor and Commonalty of the City of New Sarum to build a new Gaol within the said City, or the Suburbs or Precincts thereof, and for authorizing the Commitment of Felons and other Persons within the Limits of the said City, and the Close thereof, to the Gaol of the County of Wilts, and for explaining and amending

To prove the Allegations of the first mentioned Petition, an Act, passed in the Thirty-sixth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, "An Act for regulating the Trade and Business of Pawnbrokers," was read; the Term of which, it appeared to Your Committee, will expire at the End of the present Session of Parliament: Then,

Mr. Peter Patmore, being examined, said, That the several Regulations established by the said Act have been found beneficial to the Public; and that it would conduce to the Relief and Comfort of a numerous Class of Individuals, and to the general Benefit of the Community, if the said Act were in some Respects altered and amended, and, subject to such Alterations and Amendments, made perpetual.

To prove the Allegations of the second mentioned Petition, the said Act was again read: And,

Mr. William Gordon, being examined, said. That the said Act has been found beneficial to the Public, but that the same requires some Amendments, Alterations, and Additions, and that it would be more convenient for the Magistrates, and beneficial to the Pawnbrokers, and the Public, if the Powers of the said Act, with such Alterations, Amendments, and Additions, as may -be found requisite, were consolidated and reduced into One Act of Parliament.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, John Soane, Esquire, an Architect, being examined, said, That pursuant to several Acts of Parliament, sundry Houses, Ground, Hereditaments, and Premises, were purchased by and vested in the Petitioners, ?:nd the Edifice of the Bank was very much enlarged and extended, and the Passages leading thereto made more commodious for the Public: That, in consequence of the great Increase of Public Debt, and of the Public Business transacted by the Petitioners, and also the Extension of their Dealings and Transactions with Individuals, tire Scite on which the said Edifice now Hands is inadequate to enable the Petitioners to ereCl safe, proper, and convenient Offices for the Transaction and Management of the important Concern placed under their Management: That the Avenues leading to and adjoining the said Edifice, on the East and West Sides thereof, are narrow and inconvenient, and it is proposed to widen and render the same more commodious, and in particular to continue the West Avenue called Princes Street, in a direct Line from the Front of the Mansion House to Lothbury, and to purchase all the Premises necessary for that Purpose; and to take the Angle which will be thereby made on the East Side of such Street or Avenue, when so improved, into, and to make it Part of, the Scite of the Bank, and by that Means to increase and extend the Public Offices thereof: That the said Avenue on the West Side of the Bank, called Princes Street, is now very narrow and crooked, inso much that if the Houses on the West Side thereof, qppofite to the Bank, should take Fire, the Safety of the said Edifice would be greatly endangered; and it is therefore of great Public Importance that the said Avenue should be widened and made more commodious, and proceed in a direct Line from Mansion House Street to Lothbury: — And, the Witnesss further said. That the South End of Bartholomew Lane, opposite the South East Corner of the said Edifice, and immediately fronting the North Gate of the Royal Exchange, is very narrow and incommodious, and the Petitioners are desirous of purchasing Four Houses forming the North West Corner of the said Street called Bartholomew Lane, for the Purpose of taking down the fame, in order to widen and render more commodious the Avenue on the East Side of the Bank; and to render the said Improvement complete, it will be requisite to make a Foot Passage through the lower Part of the Tower of Saint Bartholomew's Church, adjoining to the said Houses.

A Petition of John Davis, of Duke Street, Saint George's Fields, being offered to be presented to the House;

Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer (by His Majesty's Command) acquainted thfe Floufe, That His Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House.

Then the said Petition was brought up, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioner has, after many Years

Vol. 55.

Application, and great Labour and Study, and at a considerable Expence, discovered a Method of cleaning and purifying damaged and Smutty Wheat, and rendering it fit for the Food of Man j and that the Petitioner has, in many Instances, proved the Utility and Efficacy of his Invention, and has received Testimonials thereof from the Board of Agriculture, and from many Farmers who have had Smutty Wheat converted by the Petitioner into good and Marketable Wheat; and that the Petitioner is willing to relinquish all Right and Title to the said Discovery, for the Benefit of the Public, on receiving such Recompence and Reward for the Expences he has incurred, and the Importance of the Discovery, as he shall appear to them to deserve: And therefore praying, That the House will be pleased to take his Cale into Confide ration, and grant him such Recompence and Reward as the House shall think just and proper.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

A Petition of the several Innkeepers of the City of Durham inn-Durham, was presented to the House, and read; Setting ^^‘ls Pe" forth. That the Petitioners being at all Times willing to accommodate the Public to, the utmost of their Power, and to bear their proper Share of the Burthens of the State, feel themselves uncommonly oppressed and aggrieved by the Number of Soldiers of late quartered upon them, and which has been considerably increased by the frequent Change of Stations of the Military through the Kingdom; and that, from the enormous Dearness of Provisions of every Kind, and the Inadequacy of the Government Allowance to provide for Troops on a March, the Pressure of this Grievance has become intolerable; and the Petitioners therefore beg Leave to represent the Expediency and Justice of the several principal Trades People being equally subject to the Maintenance and Support of Soldiers, as, from the Nature of their respective Trades, they partake in every Degree of the Advantage which may arise from the keeping of Soldiers, and that such a Measure (together with the Increase of Allowance) would tend greatly to lessen the Grievance of which the Petitioners complain:

And therefore praying, That the House will take into its l'erious Consideration the Subject of this Petition, and grant the Petitioners such Relief as to the House shall Item meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

A Message from the Lords, by the Clerk Assistant and the Deputy Clerk of the Crown:

Mr. Speaker,

The Lords do desire a present Conference with this House, in the Painted Chamber, upon a Subject materially affecting the Safety of His Majesty's Sacred Person, and the Happiness of His People: And also, The Lords have directed us to inform this House, That, from the Absence of their usual Messengers, and the urgent Importance of the Cafe, their Lordships had been induced to fend this Meftage by their Clerk Assistant and the Deputy Clerk of the Crown.

And then the Messengers withdrew.

ReJ'olved, That this House will fend an Answer by Messengers of their own.

And the Messengers were again called in j and Mr. Speaker acquainted them therewith.

And then the Messengers again withdrew.

Resolved, That this House doth acquiesce in the Rea-fons assigned by the Lords for fending the said Message by Vol. 55.

the Clerk Assistant and the Deputy Clerk of the Crown, instead of the usual Messengers, trusting that the lame, will not be drawn into Precedent for the future.

Resolved, That this House doth agree to a Conference with the Lords, as is desired by their Lordships; and that a Message be sent to the Lords, to acquaint them therewith.

Ordered, That the Lord Hazvkesbury do carry the said Message.

The Lord Hpwkesbury reported. That he had been with'

the Lords; and acquainted them, that this House had agreed to a Conference, as desired by their Lordships.

Ordered, That a Committee be appointed to manage the said Conference:

And a Committee was appointed of Mr. Secretary Dundas, Mr; Secretary at War, Mr. Ryder, Mr. the Lord Hawkesbury, the Master of the Rolls, Mr. Charles

Yorkc, Mr. Solicitor General, Mr fcelles, the Lord Advocate of Scotland, Mr. John , Mr. Bramston, Mr. Sloane, Mr. Thomas Pelham, Mr lace, Mr. EJlcourt, Sir Henry Paulet St. John Mildmay,

Sir Edmund Cradock Hartopp.

Then the Names of the Managers were called over 5 and they went to the Conference.

And being returned;

Mr. Secretary Dundas reported. That the Managers had met the Lords at the Conference, which was managed, on the Part of the Lords, by His Royal Highness the Prince of Wales j and that the Conference was to acquaint this House, that the Lords, in consequence of the recent most atrocious and treasonable Attempt on His Majesty's Most Sacred Person, by which His Majesty's Life, so justly dear to all His faithful Subjects, was exposed to the utmost Danger, have taken the same intd Consideration, and have agreed to an Address to be presented to His Majesty thereupon, to which Address the Lords desire the Concurrence of this House.

The House proceeded to take the said Address into Consideration.

And the said Address was read , and is as followeth; viz.

Most Gracious Sovereign,

We, Your Majesty's most dutiful and loyal Subjects, the Lords Spiritual and Temporal, 'in Parliament assembled, beg Leave humbly to approach Your Majesty's Throne, to express our Horror and Indignation at the late atrocious and treasonaBIe Attempt against Your Majesty's Sacred Person, and our heartfelt Congratulations to Your Majesty, and to our Country, on Your Majesty's happy Preservation from so great a Danger.

Attached to Your Majesty by every Sentiment which Can most endear a Sovereign to His People, by the long Experience of Your Majesty's paternal Affection towards us, by the Sense of all the Benefits which we derive from Your Majesty's just and mild Government, and by our Veneration for the distinguished Virtues which adorn Your Majesty's Character, and which are always most eminently displayed in the Hour of Trial, we acknowledge, with all Humility and Gratitude, the merciful Interposition of that Providence which has been so signally manifested on this Occasion; and we make it our carnest Prayer to Almighty God, that He will long preserve to us the same Blessings, and that He will continue to watch over and to prated a Life so justly dear to us.

Then the said Address being read a Second Time;

Resolved, Nemine Conlradicente, That this House doth agree with the Lords in the said Address to be presented to His Majesty.

And the Blank therein was filled up with the Words " and Commons."

Ordered, That a Message be sent to the Lords, to acquaint their Lord ships, that this House hath agreed to the Address to which the Lords desired the Concurrence

And the said Clause was Twice read; and, upon the Question put thereupon, agreed to by the House to be made Part of the Bill.

Another Clause was offered to be added to the Bill, directing that Compensation shall be made to Owners of Tenements, Labourers, and other Persons, if they are subject to Loss on Account of Carroons.

And the said Clause was Twice read; and, upon the Question put thereupon, agreed to by the House to be made Part of the Bill.

Then several Amendments were made by the House to the Bill.

Ordered, That the Bill, with the Amendments, be ingrossed.

Mr. Bragge, according to Order, reported from the Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred to consider of the several Acts, passed in the last Session of Parliament, relative to Duties on Income, the Resolutions which the Committee had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same were read; and areas followeth;

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Rules prescribed in the several Acts for granting Duties on Income, or by either of them, as far as relate to the Mode of ascertaining Income arising from Land occupied by the Owner, or by a Tenant at Rack. Rent, shall be repealed.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, in lieu thereof, such Income arising from Land occupied by a Tenant at Rack Rent shall be taken in the Proportions herein after specified^to the aggregate Amount of the following Articles; videlicet.

Rent for One Year payable to the Landlord.

Parochial and other Rates and Assessments charged on the said Lands, or upon the Occupiers in respect of such Lands, on the Average of the Three Years ending on the 25th Day bf March preceding, if payable by the Occupier.

The. Value of all Tythes, when taken in Kind, or the Sums paid or payable for the fame, or agreed to be paid in Satisfaction for the fame, within or for the last preceding or the current Year.

If such aggregate Amount be under Three Hundred Pounds a Year, then the Income shall be taken at Three Fifths of such Amount, and if at Three Hundred Pounds or upwards, then at Three Fourths of such Amount.

And in case of Lands occupied by the Owner, the Income arising therefrom shall be taken at the aggregate Amount of the Rent at which the same are worth, to be let by the Year, according to the ordinary Rent of Lands of the like Quality, and under the like Circumstances, in the same Neighbourhood, and Two Third Parts of what would be computed to be the Income of the Tenant at Rack Rent as above mentioned.

Resolved, That it i» the Opinion of this Committee, That it is expedient that the Provisions of the said Acts, which exempt any Person from the said Duties who shall be resident in this Kingdom for a temporary Purpose,

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Duties now payable on the Importation of Oil of Turpentine, except the Duties imposed thereon by an Act, made in the Thirty-eighth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for the better Protection of the Trade of this Kingdom, and other Purposes, do cease and determine.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Comrrfttee, That a Duty of Two Pence Halfpenny be charged upon every Pound Weight of Oil of Turpentine imported into this Kingdom, and such Duty shall be subject and liable to the additional Duty of Five Pounds per Centum, and Five Pounds per Centum, granted by Two Acts, of the Thirty-seventh Year of His present Majesty, on Goods imported.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Duties and Drawbacks now payable on Tar imported into or exported from this Kingdom, except the Duties imposed thereon by an Act, made in the Thirty-eighth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for the be tter Protection of the Trade of this Kingdom, and other Purposes, do cease and determine.

My Lords, and Gentlemen,

Poor House is situate in the Middle of the said Town, dole to the Market Place there, and, by reason of the great Increase of Buildings within these last few Years in the said Town, is now so surrounded and confined as to prevent that free Circulation of Air which is necessary lor the Health and Convenience of the Poor Persons who are kept and maintained in the said Poor House; and that the Parishioners of the said Town, at a Public Vestry of the said Parish, held the 6th Day of :anuary last, came to a Resolution to erect a new Poor Home out of the Town, instead of adding to and repairing the old One, and that Plans should be delivered in lor that Purpose, and several Plans were delivered in accordingly; and that a Piece of Land in the Neighbourhood of the said Town was con traded for, whereon to build a new Poor House, and it was the Intention of the Parishioners to have disposed of the present Poor House, and other Premises adjoining the fame, belonging to the Parish, in order to have enabled them to have completed their laid Purchase, and to have paid some Part of the Expence of building such new Poor House; but, on the Title to the said Premises being laid before Counsel by Older of the said Parishioners, they have been adviled that they cannot make a good Title to the same without the Aid and Authority of Parliament; and that such Opinion of Counsel was not given or made known to the Petitioners until after the Tune limited by the House for receiving Petitions for Private Bills: And therefore praying, That they may be at Liberty to present a Petition for Leave to bring in a Bill for effecting the above Sale and new Purchase, and for veiling the Land to be purchased in the said Vicar, Constable, Churchwardens, and Overseers, and their Successors, for the Purpose of erecting such new Poor House, and other necessary Buildings, and for the better Regulation, Management, and Employment of the Poor to be maintained therein, when the same shall nave been ere died, and for borrowing Money for the above Purposes.

Report on Mr. Mr. Peele reported from the Committee, to whom

titiln? Pc the Petition of Thomas Foden, of the City of

Chymist and Cotton Manufacturer, was referred; That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the fame, as it . appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Re-

port in his Place; and afterwards delivered the fame, together with an Appendix thereunto, in at the Clerk's Table: Where the Report was read; and is as followeth , viz.

Your Committee have, in obedience to the Orders of the House, examined the Matters referred to them, and humbly report;

That they have principally directed their Enquiries to Three Points; viz.The Nature of Mr. Foden s Discovery — The Benefits to be derived from it by the Public, and the Extent in which these Benefits may be obtained — And, the Reward to which the Inventor may be entitled. On each of these Heads they beg Leave to submit the Evidence they have received, distinctly and separately, to the Consideration of the House.

On the First Head they have examined Mr. Foden, the Inventor of the Discovery in question; who stated the Method of preparing his Composition called " Chryltalline Size," as described in the Specification of his Patent, to be as follows:

" 1 take a Quantity of calcined Gypsum, or any other calcareous or argillaceous Earth, I reduce them into a fine Powder; I then take Alum, Sugar, and the Glutine or Farina of Potatoes, these I mix together; I then, by the Addition of the Mineral Alkali and Glue, temper it to all Weathers;, and then it is made use of, in a boiled State, to form Paste, Size, or any other Purpose."

On the Second Head of Enquiry, they also examined Mr. Foden; who-delivered in to Your Committee Copies of Proceedings at several Meetings of Cotton Manufacturers, held at Manchester and its Neighbourhood, respecting his Discovery of a Substitute for Flour, for the U'c of the various Branches of the Cotton Manufactures, which Your Committee have subjoined in the Appendix to this Report. He then further stated, " That the Gypsum used in preparing his Chrystalline Size can be found in its natural State, in any Quantity, equal to Coals; the Places where it is principally found are Derbyshire, Nottinghamsh in prodigious Quantities, Cumberland, Wales, Lancashire, all a-round

tol, and in fiiort in every County of the Kingdom, was it to be fought for. That there is an earthy Substance contained in the Potatoes, which, on their being grated into Water, precipitates to the Bottom of the Vessel. One Third of this to Two Thirds of Gypsum, calcined and ground, forms the Powder of which the Paste is made, with a small Addition of Alum and Mineral Alkali, Glue, &c. That from Five Pounds of Potatoes, Ten Ounces of Glutine may be produced; that he further obtains about One Pound and Three Quarters, or Two Pounds, of Pulp, or fibrous Matter, and the Remainder is retained in the Water, from which a Spirit tan be obtained by Distillation. The fibrous Matter remaining may, with the Addition of about One Quarter of its Weight of Meal, be converted into Bread, highly Nutritive for Cattle, and will keep for Years, not ' liable to be destroyed by Frost. . That the Glutine from 9

damaged Flour, from Linseed, Horse Chesnuts, and other vegetable Substances, which contain mucous Matter, ^nd from Substances producing Animal Glue, may be applied to the same Purposes; — If Potatbes could be bought at Six Shillings per Load, or Two Shillings per Bushel, he could make One Fluttdred Weight for leis than Twenty Shillings, exclusive of the Advantages which may be derived from the Pulp and the Distillation. One Hundred Weight of this Substance will go further in making Paste, than One Hundred of fine Flour. He thinks this Powder could not be prepared by the Manufacturer without Difficulty, because the grinding of the Gypsum would require very heavy Machinery, and they might be induced to ule Lime in a Caustic State, which would be injurious to the manufactured Goods; if be was enabled to set up a Manufactory, he could supply the Public in One Month. That it takes near Two Pounds of Flour for every Piece of Cloth of Thirty Ya.ds made in this Kingdom, in the fizing, dressing, and printing of the Goods.

Your Committee next examined Doctor William king/on, ^Lecturer of Chemistry of Guy's Hospital) who stated,

" That he was acquainted with the Ingredients of which Mr. Foden's Substitute for Flour Paste is composed, and believes Mr. Foden'sStatement to be correct. He understands it consists principally of the farinaceous Part of the Potatoe, mixed with calcined Gypsum, or Selinite reduced to fine Powder; he conceives it likely to be applicable for many of the Purposes for which Paste is employed. If carefully calcined he does not conceive it to be detrimental to any Material he knows of; the Calcination is so simple a Process, that with common Care he thinks any Person may perform it; he has always understood Gypsum to be a Mineral Substance, found in different Parts of the Kingdom in great Abundance: he knows it has long been imported from France at a moderate Expence."

Dodfcor James Cutrey was next examined; and stated,

" That he believes the Gypsum found in Great , when properly calcined, is of the same Quality with that imported from France-, that by the Term Calcination applied to that Substance is merely meant the Use of such a Degree of Heat, as to expel the Water of Chryf-tallization and reduce it to a fine Powder; that the Remainder of the Potatoes, exclusive of the Glutine and the fibrous Matter, is washed off by the Water, and appears to consist of the watery Juice of the Potatoe. He thinks the Composition, if properly prepared, cannot injure the Cotton Goods, because he understands that from the Mode of its Application it does not penetrate the Substance of the Fibre of the Cotton, but is merely applied to its Outside in the Manner of a Varnish."

Mr. Williams, Callico Printer, at Stratford, in Essex was next examined; and stated,

" That as a Substitute for Paste, Mr. Foden's Composition will answer; but that he was not prepared to (peak respeefting Gum, compared with Mr. Foden's Composition, as he was making Experiments to that Effetft. The Effect of Mr. Foden's Composition is to make the Colour deeper than when Gum is used to thicken it, but the same Effect is produced by the common Paste."

Edward Stracey, Esquire, was then examined; and stated,

" That the Earth added to the Glutine in making the Paste, the Earth being as Two to One of the Glutine; whatever therefore is the Consumption of Paste, in such Proportion will be the Gain of the Food laved to Man."

Mr. Foden then stated,

" That the Weight of the extracted Glutine being added in Flour to the Pulp of the Potatoe, will restore

its

40 Geo. III. M 565

its nutritious Qualities; and it will'be more adapted to the Food of Cattle than before."

Edward Stracey, Esquire, being again examined, expressed the same Opinion.

On this Head of Enquiry Your Committee beg Leave to remark. That the Advantages proposed to be obtained from this Invention are of Four distinct Kinds: First, The Saving to the Manufactureers by the Substitution of a cheaper Article instead of Paste: Secondly, The Saving of Wheat Flour by the Employment of different Substances, of which great Part are of a Mineral Nature, for Uses in which great Quantities of it have hitherto been con fumed: Thirdly, The obtaining a considerable Quantity of cheap and nutritious Food for Cattle, from the Refuse of the Potatoes used in preparing the Chrystalline Size: Fourthly, The Use which may be made of the Water in which the Potatoes are to be mixed, for the Purpose of Distillation.

Your Committee have stated the Evidence laid before them in Support of the Expectation of the Two first of these Advantages; and it appears to them sufficient to justify very considerable Hopes of Success. With respect to the general Saving of Human Food which may be derived from it, it may, however, be proper to observe, that the Quantity of Potatoes consumed in preparing the Chrystalline Size on an extensive Scale must necessarily be very great, since Five Pounds of Potatoes produce only Ten Ounces of Glutine; but inasmuch as this may operate as a Motive for increasing the Cultivation of that valuable Root, Your Committee would not consider it as an Objection, nor can it at any Time be equivalent to the present Consumption of Wheaten Flour in Paste, as Two Thirds of the Composition of the Size is derived front the Mineral Ingredients.

With respect to the Two other Advantages held out by the Inventor, no Evidence has been adduced before Your Committee, except that several Cakes have been produced, composed of the Refuse of Potatoes, with a small Mixture of Meal from Barley, or other Sort of coarse Grain, which, from their Appearance, seemed likely to answer the Purposes intended.

With regard to the Third Head of Enquiry, Your Committee have judged that they should best execute the Intentions of the House, by laying before them such Suggestions as they have received from the Inventor himself, respedinga Mode of Remuneration, submitting' to the Wisdom of the House to decide which, if either, of the Plans proposed, may be deserving their Consideration.

The Expedations of the Petitioner will be explained by aReference to his Petition, of which Your Committee have subjoined the following Extract:

" That Your Petitioner, anxious to save the great Consumption of Wheat Flour at all Times in the various " Manufactures before mentioned, particularly at this " Period, is willing to relinquish all Right and Title to " the Interest he now has in the said Discovery, on receiving such Recompence and Reward for the heavy " Expences he has incurred, and the Time and Labour " he has bellowed, as this Honourable House shall think " just and proper.

" Y'our Petitioner therefore humbly prays thisHonourable House to take the Premises into Consideration, and " to grant Your Petitioner such Recompence and Reward " as lb useful and important a Discovery shall appear to " merit."

In addition to which, Your Committee beg Leave to subjoin the following Proposition which Mr. Foden has offered as an Alternative, instead of the Surrender of his Patent Right, and which he wishes to be adopted:

" T. Foden wishes Parliament to let him have Ten Thousand Pounds, to be inverted in Trustees ap-« pointed by Parliament, to assist him to carry on

Bull's Head Inn, Manch8 th April 1800.

At a Public Meeting of the Merchants, Manufacturers, and Printers of Manchester, and the neighbouring Towns, convened at the Requisition of the Committee appointed at a former Public Meeting, held on the 4th Day of March last, to investigate the Merits of the Difr covery made by Mr. Foden, of a Chrystalline Size and Paste, composed of Materials forming a Substitute for Flour;

C. F. Brandt, Esq; Borough reeve, in the Chair;

The Proceedings of the Meeting held on the 4th Day of last Month being read, the Committee made the following Report:

" REPORT of the Committee appointed at a General Meeting of the Merchants, Manufactureers,

Printers, Dyers, Bleachers, Sizers, &c. &c. of this Town and Neighbourhood, held the 4th of March 1800, for the Purpose of ascertaining the Merits and Properties of Mr. FodenChryftalline Size and Paste, as a Substitute in Manufacturing Purposes for Wheat Flour.

J. Silvester, Esq; Chairman.

" Your Committee having been directed to make Enquiries and Experiments upon the said Substitute for Wheat.Flour, have taken into their serious Consideration this important Subject; they have, however, directed their Views merely to the Properties and Effects, without analyzing or enquiring into their elementary and component Parts; taking for granted, that the Specification given in by Mr. Foden, upon obtaining his Patent, is a true and faithful Recital of those Fadts.

" Your Committee, deeply impressed with the great Importance of these Discoveries, especially at this particu-larCrifis, if the Properties ascribed to them could be generally ascertained, and acted upon with Effect, by the Advantages alone in abridging the large Consumption of Flour for Manufacturing Purposes, of this valuable Article, a great Blessing would be derived to this Istand, that could not fail of securing a National Reward, and well-earned Honours, to its Author.

" Your Committee have been respectively furnished with these Compositions, and a certain Proportion has been delivered to the different Artificers; viz. Sizers,

Bleachers, Weavers, Dyers, and Printers, in order the better to ascertain its Utility, and the Advantages to be derived, by their accurate Observations made upon the visible Changes and Effects produced by a proper Application, through the various progressive Stages of all these Branches of Manufacture, approximating to Maturity.

" Your Committee have witnessed many Experiments, conferred with and examined numerous Artificers; and, with little Variation (none as to the Effects), these Operations and Enquiries have been attended with complete Success; but how far their Merits and general Principles, as applicable to Manufacturing Purposes, may be further extended, would be impossible for Your Committee to ascertain, inasmuch that in many Instances the Applications have been found not only useful and ample Substitutes for Flour, but also for Starch, and have other peculiar Properties far exceeding that of either, and much more useful, when the Principle and Application is more familiarized, and better understood.

" Your Committee, the more effectually to give Weight to their Opinion, beg Leave to submit in Detail the Evidence of the respective Manufacturers who have made Trials and Experiments of this Size and Paste, and

7 E who

23 ° Mail. 1800.

Report cm Mr. Fcxlcn's Feu-tioit — renit-miuA.

who have been examined by Your Committee; with their various Productions and Specimens annexed.

" Your Committee have therefore only to add, that, from a particular Attention and minute Investigation of the Properties of this Size and Paste, are fully persuaded they will answer all the Purposes described; and from their Excellence, simple Process in the Preparation, and comparative Cheapness, they will be preferred to that of Flour or Starch, and not only lessen the Consumption, but Your Committee are decidedly of Opinion they will be found to supplant the common Preparation of making Flour-Paste, and facilitate the Operation of the Weaver, Printer, and every other Branch of Manufacture embraced by these Enquiries.

" Your Committee are also finally of Opinion, that they will prove a simple efficacious Succedaneum, eventually the Means of saving to this Nation the Consumptions of very considerable Quantities of Wheat Flour, hitherto annually consumed in this Kingdom for Manufacturing Purposes only.

(Signed)

J. Silvester, Merchant.

James Darbyshire, Manufacturer of heavy Cotton Goods.

Die above Report having being read, and it appearing to be the Wish of the Meeting that the compound Ingredients of the Chrystalline Size and Paste offered by Mr. Foden should be disclosed to the Committee, as well as analyzed and prepared by them, in order the better to ascertain its comparative Value with that of Wheaten Flour, the Gentlemen Committee attending the Meeting, having withdrawn for the above Purpose, on their Return made the following additional Report:

" In Consequence of the Request of this Meeting, We, the Undersigned, do certify, That we have purchased and prepared the component Ingredients for making the above Size and Paste, and that the same Effects have been produced on the Combination of these Materials, so purchased and prepared by us, as were the Result of former Experiments on the same Powder or Compound furnished by Mr. Foden himself; and moreover, we are sufficiently convinced, by the Simplicity of the Process, and the comparative Cheapness of the Ingredients, that this Composition will prove, for Manufacturing Purposes, an adequate Substitute for Wheaten Flour.

(Signed) J. Silvester, Chairman.

x ft. That this Meeting is highly satisfied With the Report of the Committee, and is sensible of the Benefits that will arise to the Manufacturers of this Country, by this Discovery, when generally introduced.

2d. That this Meeting recommends the Use of Mr. Foden's Chrystalline Compound to the Wcavers. Sizers of Twists, Bleachers and Finifliers of Goods, as a proper Substitute for Flour, for Size and Stiffening, as well as to the Printers for Paste.

3d. That the Thanks of this Meeting are justly due to the Gentlemen who composed the said Committee, for their laborious Investigation of the Subject entrusted to their Care, as well as for their very ingenuous and candid Report of the fame.

Mr. Bllifon reported from the Committee, to whom the Report was re-committed, which was made from the Committee to whom the Petition of the Company of Proprietors of the Horncastle Canal, in the County of Lincoln, was referred; That the Committee had further examined, and found that the Standing Orders of the House, relative to Navigation Bills, had not been complied with, because the Necessity of applying to Parliament did not arise until long after the Months of August and September, the Times limited for giving Notices; that such Necessity was occasioned by the very violent and continued Floods during the Whole of the last un-seasonable Winter, by which the Works already constructed were found to be so greatly damaged, and the Cuts to be so filled up and obstructed by Silt and Sand, that, unless the same could be repaired and removed during the ensuing Summer, the Undertaking would be in Danger of total Ruin, and the Expence would, in Consequence, be so increased, as to make it probable that the Proprietors might eventually not be able to raise Money sufficient, and that the Public would therefore be deprived of the Benefits of so useful a Navigation; that the Funds of the Company are exhausted, and they are totally unable to effectuate the Purposes without an Amendment of their Act, and Powers to raise a further Sum of Money, and to take some additional Toll, in Proportion to the very great Expence which they are thus unavoidably put to: Upon the Ascertainhuent of these Fasts, a Petition was presented to Parliament on the 10th of March last, and a General Meeting of the Company was summoned by Public Advertisement, but that, owing to the distant Residence of many of the principal Proprietors, the same was not held until the 30th Day of April, when the W aters being run off, and the Extent of the Injury and Damages done being apparent, it was unanimousty agreed, upon due Consideration of the Circumstances, to

Voi 55-

Mali, 569

apply to Parliament for Leave to bring in a Bill, in the present Session, as the only Means of averting the great Loss that mult arise to the Proprietors, the injurious Delay to Public Business, and the future increased Burthen that mult fall upon the Public by the Imposition of still heavier Tolls, to meet the additional Expence which must necessarily arise; that accordingly Notice of the Intention to apply to Parliament in the present Session for a Bill for the above Purposes was affixed on the Sessions House Door at Kirton, in the said County of Lincoln, at the last Easter Quarter Sessions, and was likewise advertised Three Times in The Lincoln, Rutland, and Stamford Mercury, on the 2d, 9th, and 16th Days of this Instant May; and that the Committee had further examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Atl Act, passed in the Thirty-fourth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for making and maintaining a Navigable Canal from the River Witham, to or into the Town of Horncastle, in the County of Lincoln, and also for amending and rendering complete the Navigable Communication between the said River Witham and the Fosdike Canal, through the High Bridget, in the City of Lincoln, was read; whereby it appeared, That the Petitioner^ and others were united and incorporated by the Name of, " The Company of Proprietors of the " Horncastle Navigation, in the County of ,"

and were thereby empowered to make the said Navigation under the several Rules, Regulations, and Direct tions, contained in the said Act, and for that Purpose to subscribe amongst themselves a Sum not exceeding £. 15,000, but if that Sum should prove insufficient,-they were empowered to raise £. 10,000 more by Mortgage of the Tolls and Duties granted by the said Act; and, in order to pay the Interest thereof, to impose and collect such Dues as therein mentioned, not exceeding Two Shillings per Ton, on such Goods, Wares, and Merchandize,s as should be carried up or down the said Navigation: Then,

Mr. Robert Clitherow, being examined, said. That the Petitioners have proceeded in the Execution of the said Act, and completed great Part of the said Works, and have expended the Whole of the Money they have raised amongst themselves, or have been able to borrow on Mortgage of the Tolls and Duties as aforesaid, and have incurred sundry Debts, and very great Arrears of Interest are payable to the original Subscribers by virtue of the said Act, and also laige Sums of Money to Proprietors of Estates for Lands cut and covered by making the said Canal: — And, the Witness further said. That to enable the Petitioners to finish the said Works, and discharge the said Debts and Arrears of Interest, it is rc-quisite that they should be enabled to raise a further Sum of Money than by the said Act they are empowered to do; and that for the said Purpose it is necessary to increase the present Tolls, and the said Act in some other Respects requires Amendment and Alteration.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for enabling the Horncastle Navigation Company to raise a further Sum of Money to complete the said Navigation, and for amending an Act, passed in the Thirty-second Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for making and maintaining the said Navigation: And that Mr. Ellison, Mr. Vyner, and Sir Gilbert Heathcote, do prepare, and bring in, the fapae.

Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer presented to the House, by His Majesty's Command,

A Paper, intituled, " Statement of Countervailing " Duties And also,

Copy of the humble Address to His Majesty of the Lords Spiritual and Tetnporal, and Commons, of Ireland, in Parliament assembled.

And the Titles of the said Papers were read.

The said Statement is preserved amongst the other Papers of this Session; and the said Address is as followeth; viz.

To the KING'S Most Excellent M A JEST Y.

The humble Address of the Lords Spiritual and Temporal, and Commons, in Parliament assembled.

Most Gracious Sovereign,

We Your Majesty's Most dutiful and loyal Subjects, the Lords Spiritual and Temporal, and Commons, in Parliament assembled, beg Leave to acquaint Your Majesty, That we have agreed to those Alterations and Additions which have been made by the Two Houses of the Parliament of Great B, to the Resolutions which we submitted to Your Majesty, in our Joint Address of the 28th of March last, as proper to form the Articles of Union of the Two Kingdoms: That we have seen with the most cordial Satisfaction, that entire Correspondence of Sentiment, which has been manifested by the Two Legislatures, in the Arrangement of this important Subject; and we doubt not, that by a Continuance of that friendly Disposition, the great Work, which occupies their Joint Attention, will be speedily and happily completed.

We beg Leave, at the same Time, to lay before Your Majesty, a Statement of those Countervailing Duties which are agreed upon as necessary to be imposed on Articles, the Growth, Produce, and Manufacture of Great Britain, imported into this Kingdom, which we humbly request Your Majesty will communicate to the Two Houses of Your Parliament of Great Britain, for their Concurrence.

(Signed) JOHN GAYER, Cler. Pari.

G. F. HILL, Cler. Dorn. Com.

Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred to consider further of His Majesty's most Gracious Message of the 2d Day of April last, communicating to this House the Resolutions of the Lords and Commons of Ireland respecting an Union between the Kingdoms of Great Britain and Ireland, with their Address to His Majesty thereupon, the Resolution which the Committee had directed him to report to the House -, which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the several Duties herein after mentioned shall be the Countervailing Duties to be paid on Importation from Ireland into Great Britain, after the Union of the Two Kingdoms, on the several Articles enumerated in the Schedule N° I. A. annexed to the Sixth Article of the Union between the said Kingdoms; viz.

And the same being read accordingly;

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill to repeal so much of the first mentioned Act as prohibits the Use of Horse Hides in making Boots and Shoes; and for better preventing the damaging of Raw Hides and Skins in the flaying thereof: And that Mr. Gascoyne,

A Petition of the Curriers, Shoemakers, Sadlers, and other Artificers concerned in manufacturing, cutting, or felling Leather in the Town and County of Northampton, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That very considerable Damage hath accrued, and long been sustained by the Petitioners, His Majesty's Revenue, and the Public in general, by the galhing and cutting of Hides and Skins in the taking off agd flaying the fame, and which the Laws now in being appear inadequate to prevent: And therefore praying for Relief in the Premises; relying that the House will frame l'uch Laws and Regulations, with such Penalties and Forfeitures, as shall seem meet, and calculated to ensure the desired End.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

And the said Order being read accordingly;

A Message from the Lords, by Mr. Holford and Mr. Graves;

Mr. Speaker,

The Lords have agreed to the Resolution of this House, relative to the Countervailing Duties to be paid on Importation from Ireland into Great , after the

Union of the Two Kingdoms, on the several Articles enumerated in the Schedule N° 1. A. annexed to the Sixth Article of the Union between the said Kingdoms, and have also agreed to an Address to His Majesty thereupon, to which they define the Concurrence of this House.

And then the- Mcfilngers withdrew.

The House proceeded to take the said Address intb Consideration.

And the said Address was read; and is as followeth; viz.

Most Gracious Sovereign,

We, Your Majesty's most dutiful and loyal Subjects, the Lords Spiritual and Temporal, in Parliament assembled, beg Leave to lay before Your Majesty a Statement of the Countervailing Duties which we have agreed upon as necessary to be imposed on Articles, the Growth, Produce, or Manufacture of Ireland, imported into Great Britain-, which we humbly request Your Majesty will communicate'to the Two Houses of Parliament of Ireland, for their Concurrence.

Then the said Address being read a Second Time;

Resolved, That this House doth agree with the Lords . in the said Address to be presented to His Majesty.

And the Blank therein was filled up with the Words " and Commons,"

Ordered, That a Message be sent to the Lords, to acquaint their Lordships, that this House hath agreed to the Address to which the Lords desired the Concurrence of this House, and have filled up the Blank therein with the Words " and Commons."

Ordered, That Mr. Douglas do carry the said Mef-

minsterCanal and Works, but, soon after the passing of the said Act, the Subscription Books were doled, and not more than a Subscription for 685 Shares admitted, at £. 100. per Share, and from thence arole a Deficiency

of Money to make and complete the said Canal; and that the cxifiing Debts of the Proprietors of the Leo-minster Canal are owing for Money advanced by Members of the Committee, on the Credit of their Canal, for the Purpose of opening a Communication between the said Coal Mine and the Borough of Leominster; and that, upon a Survey of a very able Engineer, it appears by his Report, that the Money already contributed by the Proprietors for making and maintaining the said Leominster Canal, has been expended in a very extravagant and imprudent Manner, so much 1b that the Am uni of the Sum now petitioned for by the Proprie-

tors of the Leominster Canal wopld have been sufficient; under proper Management, to have rendered the Undertaking of great Utility; and that, the Petitioners conceive, the said Act of the Thirty-finl of George the Third fully enables the Proprietors of the Leominster Canal to raise a further Sum of Money, by Calls upon theni-selves, for completing their Canal, but, under the Direction of the Persons at present conducting the Execution of the Works, there appears but little Probability of the said Canal ever being finished , and that the said Bill appears not only to contain Powers for raising Money, but also for altering and amending Two former Acts of Parliament, and will, if passed into a Law, enable the Proprietors materially to vary the Line of their Canal, and other Powers now exercised by them:

Mr. Thomas Williams reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the Mayor, Bailiffs, and Burgesses, of the Town and Borough of Carnarvon, and of the several Persons, whole Names are thereunto subscribed, being Inhabitants of the same Town, and the Neighbourhood thereof, was referred; That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition, and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Mr, Owen Anthony Poole, being examined, said, That the Church or Chapel of Saint Mary, within the said Town and Borough, and the Tower thereof, are in a very ruinous and decayed State, so as Divine Service cannot with Safety be performed therein, and it is necessary that the said Church and Tower should be taken down and rebuilt, which will be attended with considerable Expence.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for taking down, and re-building, upon a more enlarged Scale, the Chapel of Saint Mary, in the Town of Carnarvon: And that Mr. Thomas Williams and the Lord Paget do prepare, and bring in, the fame.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Powers given by the different Statutes now in Force, relative to the Repair of County Bridges, are in some Respects defective.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, T6at the Surveyors of County Bridges, appointed by Justices of the Peace at their General Quarter Sessions, should have the same Power to get, take, and carry away, Stones, Gravel, Sand, and other Materials, for the Repair of Roads over Bridges, and the Roads for the Space of Three Hundred Feet at each of the Ends thereof, as are given to the Surveyors of Highways by virtue of an Act, pafle<# in the Thirteenth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, making Satisfaction for the Damages done thereby, in the same Manner as is directed by the said Act.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Justices of Peace, in General Quarter Sessions, should be empowered to alter the Situation of County Vol. 55.

Bridges, and to widen and enlarge the fame, and the Roads, for the Space of Three Hundred Feet, at each of the Ends thereof, and to order their Surveyor to agree for the Recompence to be made for the Ground to be taken for those Purposes; and, if the said Surveyor cannot agree with the Persons, Bodies Politic or Corporate, who arefeifed and possessed of such Ground, or if they cannot be found, or shall refuse to treat or take such Recompence as shall be offered to them respectively by such Surveyor, then the said Justices shall have Power to impannel a Jury, at the Quarter Sessions, to assess the Damages to be given, and Recompence to be made to the Owners and others interested in the said Grounds, in the Manner directed by the said Act of the Thirteenth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, in respect to the widening of Highways; and, if the Jury Hull give a Verdict for more Money than was offered by the said Surveyor, the Costs of the Proceedings to be paid by the said Surveyor, but, if the Jury shall give a Verdict for no more, or for less, than was offered by the Surveyor, then the Costs to be paid by the Person or Body Corporate who refused to accept the Satisfaction so offered to him; and that, on Payment or Tender of the Money so to be awarded, on leaving it in the Hands of the Clerk of the Peace, if the Party entitled to receive it cannot be found, or shall refuse to accept it, the Interest of such Person shall be diverted out of him, saving, nevertheless, to the Owner of the Ground all Mines and Minerals which may be got without breaking the Ground, and all Timber and Wood growing on such Ground.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That it is expedient that Provision should be made for compelling such Surveyors to account for such Monies as may be received and disbursed by them, and for inflicting Penalties in the same of Neglect of Duty.

A Petition of the Merchants and Traders of London, and its Vicinity, Owners of Carts for carrying on their own Trade, whole Names are thereunto subscribed, was pretented to the House, and readj Taking Notice of the Bill for extending the Powers of Two Acts, passed in the Eighteenth and Thirtieth Years of the Reign of his late Majesty King George the Second, to prevent the Misbehaviour of the Drivers of Carts in the Streets in London, Westminster, and the Limits of the Weekly

Bills of Mortality; and Setting forth. That the Petitioners conceive such Bill is unnec^flary, and if it should pals into a Law, will be highly injurious to the Petitioners: First, Inasmuch as the Petitioners are already fub-ject to the Laws in Force for the Regulation of all Waggons, Carts, and other Carriages (not working for Hire), and these Laws have been hitherto found fully sufficient for the due Regulation of the Petitioners Carts and Waggons, and for the Correction of any Misconduct in the Drivers thereof in the City of London and its Liberties: Secondly, That Rules, Orders, and Ordinances, necellarvfor fixing the Distances, Charges, and Labour of Hired Carmen, Hackney Coachmen, and Watermen, and for regulating their Stands, Plying Places, Modes of Proceeding, and Conduit, cannot be necessary or proper for the Controul or Government of Persons keeping their own-Carts, used by them for the Purpose of expediting their own Business only, and not Handing in the Streets for Hire, any more than such Rules, Orders, and Ordinances, would be proper for, and applicable to, Persons keeping their own Coaches, or other Carriages, or Pleasure Boats: Thirdly, That the said Bill is (as the Petitioners have been informed) brought into the House at the Instance of a Body of interested Persons, called Fellowship Carmen, whose Business is working for Hire, and who are inimical to such Persons as keep Carts for the Conduct of their own Business, and aredefirous that the Petitioners should be put under Restraints, and be thereby deterred from keeping their own Carts and Waggons, which, the Petitioners are convinced, would be highly prejudicial to the Commerce of this City, the Petitioners being warranted in asserting, that the great Extension of the Trade of London has arilen from the Facility1 and easy Expence at which the Traders of London have been able to serve the Public, by the free Use of their own Carts and Waggons: Fourthly, That the Petitioners have not heard, nor do believe, that any such great Confusion,' Inconveniencies, and Injuries, as are mentioned in the said Bill to be occasioned by their Carts,- Waggons, or Drivers, do exist, but, on the contrary, the Petitioners originally let up their own Carts on Account of the Impossibility of carrying on their Business without them; and the Petitioners are fully convinced, that the Freedom with which Private Carts and Waggons are permitted to work contributes greatly to the well and speedy Clearing of the Wharfs and Warehouses, where Goods are landed and deposited; and the Petitioners apprehend, that, were they to be subjected to the Rules, Orders, and Ordinances, made for Licensed or Hackney Carmen, amongst other Inconveniencies, they would probably be limited to the carrying of only Twenty-five Hundred Weight at One Load, whereas, by Means

of well constructed and safe Waggons, substantial Carts, and strong Horles, Four Times that Quantity may be carried with the most perfect Safety, greatly to the Advantage of the Public, and of Trade in general, by the more expeditiously clearing the incumbeted Warehouses and Wharfs, and by diminidiing the Number of Cart Horses kept in London, whereby the Consumption of Corn, Hay, and Straw, is considerably lessened, an Object of Importance in these Times of Scarcity; and the Petitioners beg Leave to represent to the House, that, if this Bill should pass into a Law, and the Petitioners should thereby be restrained in the Management of their own Carts, Waggons, &c. by the same Rules, Orders, and Ordinances, as Hackney Carmen are subjected to, it will be totally impossible for the present great Trade of London to be carried on, without incalculable Disadvantages, arising from increased Expences, Loss of Time, and other Inconveniencies-. And therefore praying, That they may be heard, by their Counsel, Agents, and Wit — nelfes, against the said Bill; and that the same may not pass into a Law.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table, until the Report be received from the Committee, to whgm the said Bill is committed; and that the Petitioners be then heard, by their Counsel, Agents, and Witnesses, against the said Bill, upon their Petition, if they think fit.

Ordered, That Counsel be admitted to be heard, at the same Time, in Favour of the said Bill, against the said Petition.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, An Act, passed in the Twenty-seventh Year of the Reign of his late Majesty King George the Second, intituled, "An Act for discharging the Corporation of the Governor, " Bailiffs, and Commonalty of the Company of Conservators of the Great Level'of the Fens, commonly " called Bedford Level, from a Debt due to the Duke " of Bedford and Earl of Lincoln, and for enabling the " Proprietors of Lands in the North Level, Part of the " said Great Level, to raile Money to discharge the " Proportion of the said North Level in the Debts of " the said Corporation, and for ascertaining and appropriating the Taxes to be laid on the said North " Level, and for the more effectual draining and prelerv-' " ing the said North Level, and divers Lands adjoining " thereto, in the Manor of was read: And,

Mr. Thomas Steed Watson, being examined, said, That the several Lands and Grounds intended to be drained under the Powers and Authorities of the said Act, were thereby divided into Five Districts or Divisiorw, as therein mentioned and described: That the Commissioners acting for the Fourth District, mentioned in the said Act, have made several Cuts, Drains, and Outlets, and erected several Bridges, Mills, and Engines, and have done several other Works for draining and preserving the Lands and Grounds within the said District, and have charged the Owners and Occupiers of the Lands and Grounds therein with the several Rates or Taxes by the said Act authorized to be raised for the particular Works of the said Fourth District, and have applied and expended the same in and about the said Works, and have borrowed and taken up at Interest several Sums of Money,

and contrafted several Debts, on account of the particular Works of the said Fourth District, and that the said Rates and Taxes have been found insufficient to discharge the said Debts, and the Yearly Expences of maintaining and keeping in Repair the said Works: That the Lands and Grounds within the said Fourth District might be further greatly improved, if additional "Works of Drainage were made therein, and if a further Yearly Rate or Tax was laid on the said Lands and Grounds for discharging the Debts already incurred, and for making, maintaining, and preserving the several necessary Works of Drainage, within the said Fourth District: — And, the Wit nets further said, That the Powers and Authorities granted by the said Act have been found to be insufficient for the effectual Drainage and Preservation of the Lands and Grounds within the said Fourth District. - >

A Petition of the several Persons, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, Inhabitants of the Town of Maidenhead, in the County of Berks, through which the ancient Bath Road to London pafles, on Behalf of themselves and others, was also presented to the House, and -read; likewise Taking Notice of the said Bill; and Set-' ting forth, That the Petitioners are Proprietors or Renters of Houses and other Property situate in, or adjoining to, the said ancient Bath Road to London, between the Town of Reading and Longford, in the County of Middlesex, and, in Consequence thereof, have been at considerable Charges in the Purchase of divers Estates, and in Erections and Buildings for the Accommodation of the Public travelling and using the said Road, and for the consequent Traffick thereon; and that the present Communication between London and New Windsor is very commodious, yet, as the Road now proposed will be much nearer, it probably would, from that and other Circumstances, and particularly as the Trustees might, by the Reduction of the Tolls to be paid for passing on and over jthe said new Road, hold out an Inducement to Travellers to go by the said proposed Road instead of the said ancient Bath Road through Colnbrook, Maidenhead, and the said other Places, the Adoption of the proposed Plan of making such new Road would prove a serious Injury to the Property of the Petitioners: And therefore praying, That the House will take their same into Consideration, and not permit the said intended Bill to pass into a Law, and that the Petitioners may be heard, by their Counsel, against the fame.

A Petition of the several Persons, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, Mortgagees of the Tolls of Maidenhead Bridge, on Behalf of themselves and others, was also presented to the House, and read; likewise Taking Notice of the said Bill; and Setting forth, That, in the Year 1772, in order to improve the Communication between London and Maidenhead, and other Places, on the old Bath Road, an Act passed to empower the Mayor, Bridgemasters, and Burgesses, of the Town of Maidenhead, in the County of Berks, to build a Stone Bridge across the River Thames, near Maidenhead, for the Purpose of which a large Sum of Money was borrowed,

£. 18,500 of which now remains due and unpaid to the Petitioners and others, which Money was advanced and lent on Mortgage of the Tolls authorized by the said Act to be collected j and that, though the present Commu-toication between London and New Windsor is very com-

modious, yet, as the new Road, proposed to be made will be shorter, it would, from that and other Circumstances, and particularly if the said proposed Road should, as it might, by the Trustees, be rendered less expensive in Point of Tolls, hold out an Inducement to Travellers to quit the old Road through Maidenhead, Salt Hill, and Colnbrook; and the Petitioners are apprehendve, that, if the said Bill should pass into a Law, the Security, would be lessened, and the Tolls rendered- inadequate to answet the several Purposes of the said Act, and discharge the Interest of the Principal Money due to the Petitioners and others: And therefore praying the House to take their same into Consideration, and not permit the intended Bill to pass into a Law, and that the Petitioners may be heard, by their Counsel, against the fame.

A Petition of the Tanners, Tawers, Shoemakers, Sadlers, Curriers, and other Artificers, residing in the Town and Borough of Denbigh, who are interested in the cutting and using of Leather, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the Petitioners, and most of the Persons employed in similar Trades through the Kingdom, have, for a considerable Length of Time, suffered, and still do constantly suffer, very serious and great Losses and Injury from the wilful and negligent cutting and galhing of Hides and Skins by the Butchers and their Servants in flaying of Cattle, which the Provisions of the Act of the 9th of Queen Anne, Chapter XI, and the other Acts now in force, are not able to guard against and restrain; for although, in the 9th of Queen Anne, Section nth, there are Penalties upon every Person offering to Sale Hides or Skins which shall be wilfully or negligently gallied or cut in the flaying; videlicet, 2 s.6 d.for every Ox Hide, &c. and is. for every Calf

Skin, yet, from the Circumstance that the Leather is of treble the Value it was at that Period, those Fines now appear small; and that, as those Informations cannot be made but through the Medium of Persons who mull have Liberty to enter the Slaughter Houses or other Buildings and Premises of the Butchers, or by the Tanners, who are the Purchasers of the Hides, this good and wholesome Provision is, in Effect, rendered totally useless, and not only the Traders in Leather, but the Community at large, are very grossly injured by this Negligence and Destruction of the Article, trom these Flaws and Galhes, to an Amount that is almost incredible; and that Sheep and Lamb Skins, which are now become of general Use, and pay a considerable Duty when manufactured into some particular Kinds of Leather, are, from the great Carelessness of the Butchers and their Servants, in taking the Skins off thele Animals, becomd very lcarce, especially those that are fit to be manufactured into Roans, a very useful Kind of Leather, which pays a Duty of is. o>d. per Dozen, and which Dozen of Skins only weigh upon the Average about Ten Pounds *

prove certain Avenues adjacent thereto; and Setting forth. That the Alteration in Princes Street, if executed

in the Manner proposed, will totally prevent the.Prosecution of the Design for making a more convenient Communication from the North Road to Cornltill, comprized in the -Plan for general Improvement of the City, under the Direction of the Corporation of London, and intended to be effofted as Opportunity offers; and that, in order to avoid laying Part of the Garden behind'Grocers Hall into the Public Way, the said Street is proposed to be made narrower than at present, the North Entrance thereof reduced to the Width of Nine Feet or there- ' abouts, and arched over, whereby the Offices of the Bank will be detached and separated from each other, and the Public much inconvenienced; and that, if the said Street was carried to the Westward of the intended Extension of the Bank, and made of a proper Width, as intended by the Governor and Directors of the Bank of England, the Public Street through the Buildings of the Bank would be avoided, that Part of the City rendered much more commodious, and the Property of the Petitioners, in the said Ward, would not sustain Injury or Depreciation in Value; and that the said Bill contains divers other Powers and Provisions, the Effect of which would be highly injurious to the Petitioners: And therefore praying, That they may be heard, by their Counsel,

Agents, and Witnesses, against such Parts of the Bill as may be prejudicial to their Property, or otherwise affect them, and that the same may not pass into a Law, as it now Hands, or that the Petitioners may have such other Relief in the Premises as to the House shall seem 'meet.

Ordered, That it be an Instruction to the said Committee, that they do admit Counsel to be heard, at the same Time, in Favour of the said Bill, against the said Petition.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That certain Grants, Conveyances, and Assurances, of certain Rents within the Survey of the Chancellor and Council of His Majesty's Duchy of Lancaster, under the Seal of the said Duchy, which were by an Act, passed in' the Nineteenth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, exempted from any Stamp Duties granted by any Act or Acts then in Force, should also be exempted from the several Stamp Duties granted since the passing of the said Act.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Stamp Duty of Six Shillings and Eight Pence, granted by an Act, passed in the Thirty-seventh Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, on Copies of Indentures, Leases, or other Deeds, or Parts thereof, should cease and determine, except as to Copies which shall be made for, or for the Security or Use of, any or either of the Parties to the same Indenture, Lease, or other Deed, not having the Custody of the Original, or a Duplicate or Counterpart thereof, or in lieu of the same Indenture, Lease, or other Deed.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That there shall be charged a Stamp Duty of Six Pence upon every Skin or Piece of Vellum or Parchment, or Sheet or Piece of Paper, on which the Copy of any Indenture, Lease, or other Deed, or any Part thereof, shall be ingrossed, written, or printed, where such Copy shall be made for, or for the Security or Use of, any Person or Persons other than any or either of the Parties to the same Indenture, Lease, or other Deed, not having the Custody of the Original, or a Duplicate or Counterpart thereof, or where such Copy shall not be made in lieu of any such Indenture, Lease, or other Deed.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That all Persons who shall act as Notaries Public, orexercise the Office of Notaries, shall take out Certificates in like Manner as Notaries practising in any Court, and pay the Duties chargeable thereon.

The said Resolutions being severally read a Second Time, were, upon the Question severally put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

Ordered, That a Bill be brought in, upon the said Resolutions: And that Mr. Buxton, Mr. Rose, Mr. Long, and Mr. Bragge, do prepare, and bring in, the fame.
