Petition of Paper Company, for Leave to present a Petition.

A Petition of the several Persons, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, on Behalf of themselves and others, interestecl in an intended Manufactory, to be called, " The Regenerating Paper Company," was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That Matthias Koops being in Possession of a Discovery or Invention for extracting printing and writing Ink from printed and written Paper, and converting the Paper, from which the Ink is extracted, into Pulp, and making thereof Paper fit for writing, printing, and other Purposes, and for the foie and exclusive Exercise of which Discovery or Invention within that Part of Great Britain called,

His Majesty's Dominion of Wales, and Town of Berwick upon Tweed, for the Term of Fourteen Years, His Ma-

VX)L. 5.5.

jesty has been graciously pleased to grant His Letters Patent unto the said Matthias Koops. his Executors, Administrators, and Assigns, dated at , the 28th

Day of April last, and which Discovery the Petitioners conceive, from the present Scarcity of Rags, and con-lequently enormous Advance in the Price of Paper, is deferring of the Countenance and Support of the House; and that the Petitioners are desirous of carrying the said Invention and Discovery into Effect, by establishing Manufactories for that Purpose, but such Manufactories cannot be established without great Risk in the Undertaking, and without a very large Expence, nor can be conveniently carried on unless a considerable Joint Stock is raised for that Purpose; and that the establishing, and carrying into Effect, such a Manufactory, is the more desirable, as every Year renders the Difficulty of obtaining Paper of all Descriptions greater, and, it is much to be apprehended, that, if this Invention should not be so far encouraged as to be prosecuted with Effect, the Business of Printing, and particularly that of Newspapers, must be, in a great Degree, discontinued, the Exportation of Paper be totally annihilated, and of course the Revenue suffer a considerable Diminution, unlc-fs some other Substitute to use for a Raw Material can be resorted to j and that the Petitioners further submit, that in case the said Manufactories shall be established and carried into Effect, the Wade Paper which is now bought up by Grocers, Tobacconists, Cheesemongers, and others, will be rc-manufactured, and those Persons be obliged to use coavte new manufactured Paper, which will of Necessity greatly increase the Public Revenue; and that the Petitioners, and several other Persons, have a!readvagreed to form themselves into a Society, and to raise a Capital Stock of £.25.000, for the Purpose of establishing and carrying on the said Manufactory, but they are apprehen-five that, under the restrictive Provisoes contained in the said Letters Patent, no more than Five Persons can carry on the said Manufactory, or be jointly interested therein, without Forfeit lire of the Liberties and Advantages guaranteed by the said Letters Patent; and that great Difficulties may arise, as well in recovering Debts which may grow due to the Proprietors of the said Manufactory, as also in defending Suits or Actions which may be brought against them for any Matter or Thing relative to the said Manufactory, as by Law all the several Proprietors and Subscribers to the said Manufactory must in such same both sue and be sued, implead and be impleaded, by their several and distinct Names and Descriptions; and also, that many Persons who are not now liable to become Bankrupts within the Intent and Meaning of any of the Laws now in Force concerning Bankrupts, are likewise fearful of subscribing Money to carry on the said Manufacture, as by becoming Subscribers to, and Part Owners thereof, they may be liable tohave Commissions of Bankrupt issued against them as Traders, unless incorporated by Act of Parliament; and that the Petitioners, conceiving that the said Discovery and Invention could not be considered as complete before the Ink had been extracted from considerable Quantities of waste, written, and printed Paper, and the same rc-manufactured again intoPaperfit for Use, which has been done; but, from the Time necessarily occupied in inch Trials, the Petitioners have been unable to bring the said Invention or Discovery to such a State of Perfection as to justify their present Application to the House before the Time limited by the House for receiving Petitions for Private Bills was ex-

A Petition of the several Persons, whose Names are Petition from thereunto subscribed, being Journeymen and Workmen Journeymen, residing in and about the Cities of London and Westmin- jon and°West-Jler, was presented to the House, and read; Setting minster, for forth, That, during the last Session, an Act passed to prevent unlawful Combinations of Workmen; and that' it is therein declared illegal, directly or indirectly, to attempt to prevail upon any Journeyman or Workman to quit the Service in which he is employed; and that the said Act, by the Use of such uncertain Terms, and others of the same Nature, has created new Crimes of boundless Extent, to which are affixed Fines, Forfeitures, and Imprisonment; and that, amongst the Crimes created by the said Act, the Breach of a Private Cohtraft, by refusing to work when hired, is enumerated as One/and made punishable by discretionary imprisonment for any Time not exceeding Three Months, to the confounding of all Distinction between Public and Private Injuries; and that, in many Instances, the Crimes created by the said Act are such as will encourage wilful Perjury in Witnesses, from the great Difficulty of its being discovered, and will of Course expose the Petitioners to numberless h

false Accusations at the Pleasure of any malicious Prosecutor; and that, by the said Act, Oflkiders are deprived of a Trial by Jury, and made subject to the Decision of a single Magistrate, which, from the Securities required upon an Appeal, and the Expence of prosecuting it, will in Effect be always final, the Act having expressly declared it illegal, under heavy Penalties, to subscribe any Sum for the Support of such Expences; and that no Certiorari to remove any Proceedings under the Act is allowed; and that the same Magistrate, who has thus the uncontrouled Power over Offenders within the Act, will, in many Cafes, be enabled to fix the Rate of Wages of Journeymen and Workmen, and, upon their Refusal to work for such Wages (however inadequate to their Labour) may licence Mailers to employ in their respectiveTrades all Persons indifcriniinately, to the Detriment of those Trades, and to the utter Dedruftion of the Workmen who have served regular Apprenticeships therein; and that Offenders within the said Act are compellable to answer Questions upon Oath, notwithstanding the several Penalties (confiding of Fines, Forfeitures, and imprisonment) to which in Consequence they may become liable, and for the Discharge from which Penalties the Act has made no diffident Provision; and that, in many Parts of the said Act, the Law is materially changed to the great Injury of all Journeymen and

8 B Workmen;

Workmen; and that, if it be not repealed, it will hereafter be dangerous for the Petitioners to converse with one another, or even with their own Families; and that its immediate Tendency is to excite Distrust and Jealously between their Mailers and them, and to destroy the Trades and Manufacture? it purports to protest: And therefore praying, That the said Act may be repealed, or that the House will give such other Relief as it shall think lit.

A Petition of the several Persons, whole Names are thereunto subscribed, being Labourers, Mechanics, and Artificers, of the Town and Neighbourhood of in the County of Latte after, was also presented to the House, and read; likewise taking Notice of the said Act; and Setting forth. That the Petitioners were not informed of the said Act till it was actually passed into a Law, whereby they were precluded from praying the House, by themselves, or Agent'?, against the fame; and that the said Act appears to the Petitioners to have created new Crimes, of so indefinite a Nature, that no one Journeyman or Workman will be safe in holding any Convenation with another on the Subject of his T/ade or Employment; and that the Petitioners and others are, by the said Act, deprived of a Trial by a Jury of their Country, and to be tried by One Justice of the Peace, who, for the most Part, is engaged in Trade, and whom, in all Cases, it is competent to the Mailers ' to feieft, but the Parties nevertheless are not even permitted to remove any Conviction by such Justice, under the said Act, by Certiorari, or any other Writ or Process whatsoever, into any of His Majesty's Courts of Record at Westminster; and that, although a Right of Appeal

is given by the said Act against any Conviction by such Justice to the General or Quarter Sessions of the Peace, yet the Sureties and Recognizance required, and the great Expence of such Appeal, puts that Remedy beyond the Reach of the Petitioners, and other Workmen, who earn, by their daily Labour, barely sufficient to maintain themselves and Families; and the said Act expressly forbids, under a severe Penalty, any Person from subscribing or'contributing any Sum or Sums of Mon y whatsoever, for the Purpose of paying any Expences incurred, or to be incurred, by any Person charged with having afte<J contrary to the Provisions of the said Act; and that, for these and- other Reasons, it is to be feared that the said Act will tend to dil'unite, more than ever yet they were disunited, Mailers and Workmen, and that the same is, in other Respects, injurious and of-preffive to the Petitioners, and other Workmen, and may therefore ultimately be productive of Evils which may prove materially injurious to the Trade and Manu-fastures of the Country; and that the said Act empowers Trustees, Treasurers, Collectors, Receivers, and Agents, to give up, in Breach of their Trust, all Monies in their Hands, Custody, or Power, and indemnifies them, in so doing, before any Court of Law or Equity shall have pronounced on the Legality or illegality of the Purposes for which such Funds shall havfe been entrulled to them; and, finally, the "Petitioners crave the most serious Attention of the House to that Part of the said Act, whereby all Persons who shall be charged with having offended against the fame, are compellable to answer, upon Oath, all Questions that shall be put to them, notwithstanding any Penalty or Forfeiture, as the Act itself expressly states, to which such Persons may be liable in Consequence of any Discovery which may be fought thereby: And therefore praying, That the said Act, or so much thereof as to the House shall seem meet, may be repealed.

And the said Petitions were severally ordered to lie upon the Table.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Letters Patent, dated the 28th Day of April last, granting to Mr. Matthias Koops, for Fourteen Years, the foie and exclusive Exercise of his Invention for extracting, printing and writing Ink from printed and written Paper, and 'converting the Paper, from which the Ink is extracted, into Pulp, and making thereof Paper fit for Writing, Printing, and other Purposes, was produced to Your Committee: Then,

Mr. Thomas Burton, a Printer, being examined, laid, That he conceives, from the present Scarcity of Rags, . > 2nd consequent enormous Advance in the Price of Paper, the Discovery of Mr. Koops will be attended with moll material Adyantage to the Public, and is deserving the Countenance and Support of this House: , Then,

VOL. 55. ‘ -

Mr. Elias Carpenter, a Paper Maker, being examined,' said, That several Persons are defirOus of carrying tbi»

Invention and Discovery into Effect, by establishing Ma-nufaftories for that Purpose, but that such cannot be "

established without great Risk in the Undertaking, and without a very large Expence; nor can it be conveniently carried on unless a considerable Joint Stock is raised. for that Purpose; and that the establishing and carrying into Effect such Manufactories is the more desirable, as every Year renders the Difficulty of obtaining Paper of all Descriptions greater j and it is much to be apprehended, that if this Invention should not be so far encouraged as to be prosecuted with Effect, the Business of Printing, and particularly that of Newspapers, must be in a great Degree discontinued; the Exportation of Paper be totally annihilated, and of course the Revenue suffer a considerable Diminution, unless some other Substitute, to use fora Raw Material, can be resorted to: —

And, being further examined, he said. That in case these Manufactories shall be established and carried into Effect,.a very large Proportion of the Waste Paper which is now bought up by Grocers, Tobacconists, Cheesemon-gers, and others, will be re-manufactured; and those Persons obliged to consume coarse new manufactured Paper, which will of Necessity greatly increase the Public Revenue: Then,

Mr. Samuel Lifter, being examined, said, That several Persons have already agreed tp form themselves into a Society, and to raise a Capital Stock of25,000, for the Purpose of establishing and carrying on the said Manur factory, but that such Persons who have agreed to subscribe and raise the said Capital Stock, are appfehensive, - . -that under the restrictive Provisoes contained in the Letters Patent, no more than Five Persons can carry on the said Manufactory, or be jointly interested therein, without Forfeiture of the Liberties and Advantages guaranteed by the said Letters Patent; and that great Difficulties may arise as well in recovering Debts, which may grow due to the Proprietors of the said Manufactory, as also in defending Suits or Actions which may be commenced or brought against the said Proprietors, for any

Matter or Thing relative to the said Manufactory, as by Law all the several Proprietors and Subscribers to the said Manufactory must in such same both sue' and be sued, implead and be impleaded, by their several and distinct Names and Descriptions; and also, that many Person$ who are not now liable to become Bankrupts, within the Intent and Meaning of any of the Laws now in Force concerning Bankrupts, are fearful of subscribing Money to carry on the said Manufacture, as by becoming Subscribers to and Part Owners thereof, they may be liable to have Commissions of Bankruptcy issued against them as Traders, unless incorporated by Act of Parliament.

A Petition of the several Persons, whose Names are Petition from thereto subscribed, being Journeymen Cotton Spinners, &0cufMan-Callico Printers, Fustian Cutters, Machine Makers, and chester, for others, working within the Town of Manchejlein the County of Lancaster, and Ten Miles round the fame, was

presented to the House, and read 5 Taking Notice of an Act, passed in the last Session of Parliament, to prevent unlawful Combinations of Workmen; and Setting forth.

That the said Act appears to the Petitioners to have created new Crimes, of so indefinite a Nature, that no Journeyman or Workman will be lafe in holding any Conversation with another on the Subject of his Trade or Employment, and that the Petitioners and others are, by the said Act, deprived of a Trial by a Jury of their Country, and to be tried by Justices of the Peace, who, in the Town and Neighbourhood o are for the moll Part engaged in Trade, and whom in all Cases 1 it is competent in the Mailers to feleci, but the Parties nevertheless are not even permitted to remove any Conviction by such Justices under the said Act, by tiorari, or any Writ or Process whatever, into any of His Majesty's Courts of Record at WeJi.nirJLr; and that, although a Right of , Appeal is given by the said Act, against any Conviction by such Justices, to the General or Quarter Sessions, yet the Sureties and Recognizance required, and the great Expence of such Appeal, puts that Remedy beyond the Power of the Petitioners and other Workmen, who.earn by their daily Labour barely sufficient to maintain themselves and Families; and the said Act expressly forbids, under a severe Penalty, any Person from subscribing or contributing any Sum or Sums of Money whatever for the Purpose of paying any Expences incurred, or to be incurred, by any Persons acting contrary to the Provisions of the said Act; and that, for these and other Reasons, it is to be feared that the said Act will tend to create Ill-will between, and dif-unite more than ever yet they were disunited, the Mailers and Workmen, and the same is in other Respects injurious and oppressive to the Petitioners and other Workmen, and may therefore ultimately be productive of Evils which may prove materially injurious to the Trade and Manufactures of the Country; and that the said Act empowers Trustees, Treasurers, Collectors, Receivers, and Agents, to give up, in Breach of their Trull, ali Monies in their Hands, Custody, or Power, and indemnifies them in so doing, before any Court of Law or Equity shall have pronounced on the Legality or Illegality of the Purposes for tyhich such Funds shall have been intrusted to them; and, finally, the Petitioners crave the moll fe-rious Attention of the House to that Part of the said Act whereby all Persons, charged with having offended against the fame, are compellable to answer upon Oath all such Questions as shall be put to them, notwithstanding any Penalty or Forfeiture, as the said Act expressly Hates, to which such Persons may be liable, in consequence of any Discovery which may be fought thereby: And therefore praying. That the said Act may be repealed, and that they may be heard by their Counsel, respecting their several Grievances, and such Relief granted as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

Mr. Stanley reported from the Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred to consider of the Report which was made from the Committee, to whom the Petition of Thomas Foden, of the City of Coventry, Chy-mist and Cotton Manufacturer, was referred, the Resolution which the Committee had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; vizi

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Discovery made by Mr. Thomas Foden, of a Chrystalline Size and Paste from Vegetable and Mineral Substances, as a Substitute for Wheat Flour in all Purposes of Manufacture where Wheat Flour is used, is likely to be attended with most important Advantages to this Kingdom, and may save the Use of Wheat Flour to a very considerable Extent.

The said Resolution being read a Second Time, was, upon the Question put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

Resolved, That an humble Address be presented to His Majesty, humbly to lay the said Resolution before His Majesty; and to request that His Majesty will be graciously pleased to direct such further Enquiry to be made on the Subject as shall be necessary for ascertaining, whether the Ingredients for making the said Substitute can be furnished in sufficient Quantities, and at such reasonable Prices, as to afford a Supply equal to the Consumption which may be required for the various Manu-fadures in which it may be useful; and, in case it shall appear that the said Discovery can be carried to such an Extent as to be of considerable National Advantage, to order such Sum to be advanced to the said Thomas Foden for that Purpose as His Majesty shall judge proper; and to assure His Majesty that this House will make good the fame.

Ordered, That the said Address be presented to His Majesty, by such Members of this House as are of His Majesty's most Honourable Privy Council.

Ordered, That a Copy of the Report, which was made from the Committee, to whom the said Petition of Thomas Foden was referred, be humbly laid before His Majesty at the same Time with the said Address.

Mr. Davis's Petition, rci spetting Smut^ ty Wheat, reported.

4© Geo. III.

i 70 J

661

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Mr. Join Davis, being examined, laid. That he has been

about Five Years, with great Application and considerable Expence, in bringing to Perfection his Method of cleaning and purifying damaged and Smutty Wheat, and rendering it fit for the Food of Man: That he has, in many Instances, proved the Utility and Efficacy of his Invention, and has received Testirtionials thereof from the Board of Agriculture, and from many Farmers who have had Smutty Wheat converted into good and Marketable Wheat: — And, the Witnesss produced to Your Committee, an Extract from the Minutes of the Board of Agriculture, dated 29th 1798;

and said. That, owing to the advanced Price in the Raw Material of which the Powder he makes use of is prepared, the Expence of cleaning a Load of Wheat now, would be more than is stated in those Minutes: — And, he added. That he is willing to relinquish all Right and Title to'his Discovery for the Benefit of the Public, on receiving such Recompence and Reward for the Expence he has incurred, and as the Importance of his Discovery shall appear to deserve: — And, the Witness being further examined, said, That Two Men can clean Forty Bushels of Wheat a Day with One Machine: That the Expence of his Powder to clean a Load of Wheat is about Fourteen Shillings in Summer, and Seventeen Shillings in Winter: That the Materials of which his Powder is made, can be procured in all Parts of the Country, and that every Person will be able to prepare it with the greatest Ease; and that it is perfectly harm lets, both to Mah and Bcaft: That the Quantity of Powder to clean a Load of Wheat will weigh from about Sixty to Eighty Pounds, and that the same Powder will do again to clean more Wheat, losing about One Half in cleaning each Load: That the Price of the Machine may , be about Ten Guineas: That the Preparation of the Powder, when at Fourteen Shillings and Seventeen Shillings for the Load of Wheat, will coll Seven Shillings in Summer^and Eight or Nine Shillings in Winter: — And, being asked, if he knew whether any of the Wheat cleaned by him had been Town, and what Sort of Wheat it produced ? he laid. He did not know whether any of it had been sown or not; his only Object having been to make the Wheat, when smutty, good and fit for Food: — Then,

John Mackaness, Esquire, being examined, said, That Mr. Davishad cleaned Wheat for him: That at one Time

he cleaned about a Peck, about One-third of which was very smutty: That Two Samples of this were taken to Market, One smutty, the other clean j. lor the Smutty Wheat a Mealman offered 12. the Load, and for the other £. 16. 16 s.:That he afterwards had Eight

Quarters cleaned, which fold for £ 18. 55. the Load: That the Method practised by Mr. Davis seemed perfectly easy, and was very expeditious: And, the Witness

added. That he knew several Farmers who have had Wheat cleaned by Mr. Davis, and that they had all expressed their highest Satisfaction with the Manner of its being done: — Then,

A Member present informed Your Committee, That lie had leen the Process of Mr. s Method of

cleaning Smutty Wheat: That he had seen Haifa Bushel of Smutty Wheat put into his Machine, and delivered therefrom in the Spate of Ten Minutes perfectly clean, and the Smell scarcely perceptible: That a Portion of it so cleaned was immediately put into a Bag and sealed up, and carried by him- to Mr. s Mill, and there

ground in his Presence, the Broad Bran only taken out; and that he had it afterwards baked, which produced Bread, to all Appearance and Taste, perfectly sweet and wholesome: That the Process was extremely easy, and by no Means laborious, and that Women might perform the Operation as well as Men: Then the several Samples of the Wheat, mentioned by the said Member, from jt6 smutty State to that of the Bread, were produced to Y'our Committee, which proved to their Satisfaction the Vol. 55.

great Benefit which might result from Mr. Ddvis's Invention being publickly known.

Present,

Read a Letter from Mr. Robinson, His Majesty's Bailiff, on Mr. Davis's Method of cleaning Smutty Wheat, and attended the Experiment; Mr. Davis being in waiting, in Nine Minutes he cleaned the Wheat received from His Majesty's Farm, foas to make it saleable at a common Price; but Friction, in the same Degree, without his Powder, would not have the EffeCL Mr. Davis informed the Board, that the Expence of cleaning a Load would not, to a Farmer, with proper Conveniencies, cost more than 7 . 6

The Secretary received Instructions from the President to shew the Samples to a Mealman; he had an Opportunity of laying them directly before Mr. Joseph Bell, Miller, Flour Factor, and Baker, of N° 86, Watling Street, who, on examining them carefully, pronounced that the Black Wheat was not worth more than 35 a Quarter; that the Sample treated with Friction only, was worth 40^. but still fit only for Blues, of which Gingerbread is made; but that the Sample fully wrought with Mr. Davis's Powder was a very-good Sample of Wheat, and now worth about 54 s.a Quarter.

Resolved, That it appears to the Board that the Discovery of Mr. Davis is very easily practicable on any Scale, effective, highly useful and important, and that he deserves the Encouragement of all Farmers.

GEORGE R.

His Majesty being informed that Doubts have arisen, touching the Powers veiled in His Majesty to dispose of certain Estates purchased by His Majesty, and alib concerning the Powers of His Majesty, and His Successors, to dispose of such Real Property as they may hereafter purchase, or may become entitled to otherwise, than by Descent with the Crown, and also touching the Application of, and Succession to, such Personal Property as His Majesty and His Successors may be entitled to at the Time of His or their Demise; and that Doubts have also arisen touching the Powers vested in the Queen to dispose of certain Estates purchased by

Her Majesty, as well as the general Powers of the Queen Consort to dispose of Real and Personal Property; and His Majesty being also informed, that, by reason of the Restrictions imposed on the Alienation of the Crown Lands, Difficulties have arisen where Lands escheated to His Majesty have been subject to Trulls or Charges, and that, in other Cafes, Inconveniences may arise from such Restrictions; His Majesty recommends to His faithful Commons to take these Subjects into their Consideration, and to make such Provisions concerning the lame, as may appear to them to be proper.

R.

A Petition of the several Persons, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, being Journeymen and Workmen redding in and about the City of Bristol: And also,

A Petition of the several Persons, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, being Journeymen and Workmen redding in and about the Borough of Plymouth: And also,

A Petition of the several Persons, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, being Journeymen and Workmen redding in and about the City of Bath;

Were severally presented to the House, and read j Taking Notice of an Act, passed in the last Sef-Vo1" 55-

(ion of Parliament, to prevent unlawful Com-, binations of Workmen; and Setting forth, That if is therein declared illegal, directly or indirectly, to attempt to prevail upon any Journeyman or Workman to quit the Service in which he is employed; and that the said Act, by the Use of such uncertain Terms, and others of the same Nature, has created new Crimes of boundless Extent, to which are affixed Fines, Forfeitures, and Imprisonment; and that, amongst the Crimes created by the said Act, the Breach of a Private Contraft, by refudng to work when hired; is enumerated as one, and made punishable by Discretionary Imprisonmerit, for any Time not exceeding Three Months, to the confounding of all Distinction between Public and Private Injuries; and that, in many Instances, the Crimes created by the said Act are such as will encourage wilful Perjury in Witnesses from the great Difficulty of its being discovered, and will of course expose the Petitioners to numberless falle Accusations at the Pleasure of any malicious Prosecutor; and that by the said Act Offenders are deprived of a Trial by Jury, and made subject to the Decision of a Angle Magistrate, which from the Securities required upon an Appeal, and the Expence of prosecuting it, will in Effect be always, final, the Act having expressly declared it illegal, under heavy Penalties, to subscribe any Sum for the Support of such Expences; and that no Certiorari to remove any Proceedings under this Act is allowed; and that the same Magistrate, who has thus the uncontrouled Power over Offenders within this Act, will in many Cafes be enabled to fix the Rate of Wages of Journeymen and Workmen, and upon their Refusal to work for such Wages (however inadequate to their Labour) may licence Masters to employ in their respective Trades all Persons indiscriminately, to the Detriment of those Trades, and to the utter Destruction of the Workmen who have served regular Apprentice-ships therein; and that Offenders within the said Act are'.compellable to answer Questions upon Oath, notwithstanding the several Penalties (confiding of Fines, Forfeitures, and Imprisonment) to which, in consequence, they may become liable, and for the Discharge from which Penalties the Act has made no sufficient Provision; and that, in many Parts of the said Act, the Law is materially changed, to the great Injury of all Journeymen and Workmen; and that, if it be not repealed, it will hereafter be dangerous for the Petitioners to converse with one another, or even with their own Families; and that its immediate Tendency is to excite Distrust and Jealously between their Masters and them, and to destroy the Trades and Manufactures it purports to protest: And therefore praying. That the said Act may be repealed, or that the House will give such other Relief as it shall think fit.

And the said Petitions were severally ordered to lie upon the Table.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the Duties of Excise now' payable for or in respect of Stills used for distilling Low Wines or Spirits, and for rectifying, compounding, or mixing. Spirits for Con- fumption, in that Part of Great Britain called Scotland,

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Duty of Two Pence Halfpenny be charged upon every Gallon of Worts or WaQi, brewed or made in that Part of Great Britain called Scotland, for extracting Spirits from Melasses or Sugar, for Consumption therein.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Duty of Two Pence Halfpenny be charged upon every Gallon of Worts or Wash, brewed or made in that Part of Great Britain called Scotland, for extracting Spirits from other Foreign Materials, for Consumption therein.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That a Duty of Three Shillings be charged upon every Gallon of Spirits distilled in that Part of Great Britain called England, and imported into that Part of Great Britain called Scotland.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That it is expedient that Two Acts, made in the Thirty-eighth and Thirty-ninth Years of the Reign of His present Majesty, for the Regulation of the Distilleries in that Part of Great Britain called Scotland, which were to continue in Force until the 10th Day of November x8oo, should be further continued.

Mr. Speaker resumed the Chair.

Mr. Bragge reported from the Committee, That they had gone through the Bill, and made several Amendments thereunto; which they had directed him to report, when the House will please to receive the same.

Ordered, That the Report be now received. 1

Mr. Bragge accordingly reported from the said Committee, the Amendments which the Committee had made to the Bill, and which they had directed him to report to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered the Bill, with the Amendments, in at the Clerk's Table: Where the Amendments were Once read throughout; and then a Second Time, One by One; and, upon the Question severally put thereupon, were agreed to by the House.

Ordered, That the Bill, with the Amendments, be ingrafted.

Ordered, That the said Bill be read the Third Time upon Monday Morning next, if the said Bill shall be then ingrafted.

A Petition of James Haig, of near,

Dihiher, and of the other Subscribers, Distillers in the Lowlands of Scotland, was presented to the House, and read; Taking Notice of the said Bill; and Setting forth, Thwt they must be materially affected by the lame, if passed into a Law, in the Form in which it now appears; and that the Incaale of the Licence Duty upon the Contents of the Still, as proposed by the Committee of the House, is a Regulation to which they would readily con-lent, provided it was not proposed at the same Time to subject them to Survey, to limit them to the Quantity 8

to them, by imposing certain other Duties upon Walh; and also, that the System now proposed will be productive of much Loss and Inconvenience to the fair Manufacturer, and mud afford innumerable Opportunities to the illicit Trader to evade the Law; and the Petitioners hope, that the House will relieve them from the ruinous Consequences which mull ensue from those Regulations, and confine the puty to a Licence upon the Still, conformable to the System formerly adopted: But, if the House should be of Opinion, that the System of Taxation by a Licence cannot be continued in thefimple Form in which it was first imposed, the Petitioners pray, That they may be restored to their original Situation, and be placed on the same Footing with the Distillers in England, that the same Mode of Taxation, and Regulations in respect to the Distilleries, may take place in both Countries, as well as a free Communication of Markets to all Parts of the United Empire, which they apprehend to be their Right by the Articles of Union between England and Scotland, and also that they may be

heard, by themselves or Counsel, against such Parts of the said Bill as affect them.

That His Majesty be enabled to direct the Sum of Sixty-five Thousand Pounds to be issued, out of the Consolidated Fund, for the Purpose xof erefling a Lazaret te on Chetney Hillin the County of with ne-

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That there be charged for every Ton Burthen of every Ship or Vessel, the Cargo of which, or any Part thereof, shall have performed Quarantine in this Kingdom, and which shall have arrived from any Part of Turkey, or from any Port or Place in , within the of Gilbraltar, or in The West Barbary on the Atlantic Ocean, with a clean Bill of Health, a Duty of Seven Shillings and Six Pence.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That there be charged for every Ton Burthen of every such Ship or Vessel, which shall have so arrived without a clean Bill of Health, a Duty of Fifteen Shillings.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That there be charged for every Ton Burthen of every Ship or Vessel, the Cargo of which, or any Part thereof, shall have performed Quarantine in this Kingdom, and which shall have arrived from any Port or Place whatever, except from any Part of , or from any Port or Place in Africa, within the Straights of Gibraltar, or in The West Barbary on the Atlantic Ocean, with a clean Bill of Health, a Duty of Three Shillings.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That there be charged for every Ton Burthen of every ' such Ship or Vessel, which shall have lo arrived without a clean Bill of Health, a Duty of Ten Shillings.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That there be charged for every Ton Burthen of every Ship or Vessel, the Cargo of which, or any Part thereof, shall consist of Goods, Wares, or Merchandize, the Growth, Produce, or Manufacture of Turkey, or of any Port or Place in Africa within the Streights of Gibraltar, or' in The West Barbary on the Atlantic Ocean, which shall have performed Quarantine in this Kingdom, and which shall have arrived from any Port.or Place in Holland, or from any Port or Place whatever at which there is not a regular established Lazarette for the Performance of Quarantine, a Duty of Seven-Shillings and Six Pence.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That there be charged for every Ton Burthen of every Ship or Vessel, which shall have so arrived under such Circumstances as shall induce His Majesty, by and with the Advice of His Privy Council, to subject them to like Quarantine as Ships arriving from Turkey without clean Bills of Health, a Duty of Fifteen Shillings.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That there be charged for every Ton Burthen of every Ship or Vessel, the Cargo of which, or any Part thereof, shall have performed Quarantine in this Kingdom, and which Ship or Vessel shall enter inwards in the Port of London, an additional Duty of One Shilling.

Resolved, That-it is the Opinion of this Committee, That it is expedient that the several Laws now in force for the Performance of Quarantine should be amended and made more effectual.

The said Resolutions. being severally read a Second Time, were, upon the Question severally put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

GEORGE R.

His Majesty acquaints the House of Commons, that Conventions have been entered into by His Direction, with the Hereditary Stadtholderof the United Provinces, for placing, at His Majesty's Disposal, certain Ships of War and Seamen, together with a Body of Land Forces, which, in consequence of their submitting to the Authority veiled in his Serene Highness, as Captain General and Admiral of the Union, had been passed over to this Country. His Majesty has given Orders, that Copies of these Conventions should be laid before Parliament and He recommends to this House to consider of such Provisions as may be necessary to enable His Majesty to fulfil the Engagements He has entered into with his Serene Highness, and to avail Himself of the Service of the said Ships, Seamen, and Troops, for the further Prosecution of the War, or in such Manner as His Majesty may think proper, for the Interests of this Country.

TERMS on which His Majesty has agreed to take into his Employment the Dutch Ships of War which surrendered to His Majesty's Fleet under the Command of Vice Admiral to be held for the Orders of his Serene Highness the Prince of Orange, in the Vlieter, on the 30th of August 1799.

I.

His Serene Highness engages, on the Behalf of the lawful Government of the Republic of the United Provinces, to furnish the Ships mentioned in the Margin , completely officered, manned, and vidtuajled, to be employed under His Majesty's Orders, in the European Seas only, and for the Advantage of the Common Cause, during the present War; or until the lawful Government of the Republic shall be re-established - therein, and shall reclaim those Ships. His Serene Highness is to be at Liberty to employ any Dutch Seamen now on board

the Minerva; or any other Dutch Seamen well affected to the lawful Government of the United Provinces, and who may he disposed to serve in the Manner and on the Terms now proposed.

II.

His Serene Highness agrees to place at the Disposal of His Majesty the Ships mentioned'in the annexed Schedule, in the State in which they now are, to be employed as His Majesty shall judge proper, and for the Benefit of the Common Cause, within the European Seas, during the War, or until the lawful Government of the Republic shall be re-established therein, and shall reclaim those Ships.

III.

In order to enable his Serene Highness to carry into Effect the Stipulation of the First Article, His Majesty engages to defray the Expence of putting the Ship of the Line, Two Frigates, and Sloop therein mentioned, into a Condjti&n for Service, and to keep them constantly in a proper State of Repair, and to supply them vith such Naval Stores as may from Time to Time be necessary for their Life while so employed as above.

IV.

His Majesty engages to cause to be paid from Time to Time to his Serene Highness, or to any Person properly authorized by him, such Sum or Sums of Money as may be requisite for the Payment of the Wages of the Officers and Crews of the said first mentioned Ships, and for their Support and Maintenance j the Amount of such . Wages and Allowances to be computed according to the Rates allowed for Ships of the like Class, under the ( Regulatipqs established in the Admiralties of the United Provinces previous to the Year 1795. The first Payment of Wages and Allowances to be made in Advance within the Space of Ten Days from the Date of the Signature of this Agreement, and from thenceforth in regu-. lar Proportions every Three Months during the Period in which the said Ships shall continue to be so employed.

V.

His Majesty engages that the said Ships and Sloop shall, at the Conclusion of the present War, be delivered up to his Serene H ighness on the Behalf of the lawful Government of the United Provinces, provided that at that Period the said Government shall be re-established in those Provinces, and that the same shall be delivered from the Power of the French.

VI.

In the Event of His Majesty's employing any of the ' Ships specified in the Schedule which is referred to in the Second Article, His Majesty engages to restore them as above to His Serene Highness on the Behalf of the lawful Government of the United Provinces, in as perfect a State as they at present sire. With a View to the fulfilling this Stipulation, His Majesty will appoint proper Persons to examine, in Conjunction with such Persons as may be nominated by his Serene Highness, and prepare Estimates of the Value of the Ships above mentioned, before they are employed; and in case any of the said Ships shall be taken by the Enemy, or be loft while employed by His Majesty, the Value thereof shall be deposited in the Hands of his Serene Highness for and in Behalf of the lawful Government of the United Provinces as above, or subject to such other Disposition as may be made thereof by any subsequent Agreement.

VII.

It is agreed, that proper Commissions to the Officer? serving on board of the Ship of the Line, Two Frigates, and Sloop before mentioned, shall be granted by His Majesty in the same Manner as they are now granted to the Officers of His Majesty's Naval Service; and that the said Officers shall also be furnished with Commissions

vf the same Rank and Date by the Prince of as

(Signed) March 11, 1800.

FIRST EXPLANATORY ARTICLE.

It is agreed that the Expression contained in the Sixth Article of the foregoing Convention, " In as per- " fect a State as they at present are," is not to be so understood as to oblige His Majesty to make Compensation for such Damage as may arise only from the reasonable Wear and Tear' of the Ships referred to in the above mentioned Article, during the Period in which they may be employed in the Manner mentioned in th<? Convention.

(Signed) W. Prince of Orange.

April 2d, 1800.

t

Approved.

By His Majesty's Command,

(Signed) Grenville.

SECOND EXPLANATORY ARTICLE.

Whereas, since the signing of the Convention of the I ith of March last, containing the Terms on which His Majesty has agreed ‘ to take into His Employment the Dutch Ships of War which surrendered at the Vlieter to His Majesty's Fleet under the Command of Vice Admiral Mitchell, several Difficulties have occurred with regard to the best Means of carrying that Agreement into Execution; especially that Part of it, by which it has been stipulated — In the First Article, That his Serene Highness engages on the Behalf of the lawful Government of the Republic of the United Provinces, to furnish the Ships mentioned therein, completely victualled; — and in the Fourth Artide, That His Majesty engages to cause to be paid, from Time to Time, to his Serene Highness, or any Person properly authorized by him, such Sum or Sums of Money for the Payment of the Support and Maintenance of the Officers and Crezvs of the said Ships, the Amount of such Allowance, to be computed according to the Rates allowed for Ships of the like ClaJ's under the Regulations established in the Admiralties of the United Provinces previous to the Year 1795:

And as those Difficulties have been found to be of such a Nature as to render another Mode of proceeding

in

25° Junit.

699

40 Geo. III.

in this Respect more eligible for the Furtherance^ the Public Service:

It is agreed, that the aforesaid Stipulations, as far as they relate to the Mod£ of Victualling the above Ships, shall be considered as making no Part of the said First and Fourth Articles of the above Convention; and in order to provide now for the fame, His Majesty engages to cause the said Ships of War to be vidualled from Time to Time in the same Manner as is practised with regard to the Crews of His Majesty's Ships of War.

(Signed) W. Prince of Orange.

London, June 10th, 1800.

Approved.

By His Majesty's Command,

(Signed) Grenville.

TERMS for receiving the Dutch Troops of his . Serene Highness the Prince of , under the Command of his Serene Highness the Hereditary Prince of Orange, info His Majesty's Service.

The King agrees to take into His Service the Troops under his Serene Highness the Hereditary Prince of Orange on the following Terms:

VII,

DESCRIPTION tie Recruit.

Each Recruit to be enlisted for Seven Years, to be examined by a Surgeon, who is to give a Certificate, signed by himself, of his Capacity or Incapacity to serve, to be Five Feet and Four Inches high, and from Sixteen to Forty Years of Age, and finally to be approved of and accepted by the Military Commissary.

VIII.

BOUNTY for Recruits hereafter to he rerifed

The Sum of Twelve Pounds will be allowed for each Recruit of the above Description, delivered at the Depot in the Isle of Wight, who shall be approved of, in Addition to which the same Bounty as specified in Article V. for the Purpose of providing the Necessaries as therein referred to, shall be made. In all, for each Infantry Recruit Fourteen Pounds Ten Shillings and for each Yager the Sum of Fifteen Pounds.

IX.

GOVERNMENT not to incur any additional Expence.

It is to be clearly understood that the Government is not to incur any Expence for a rejected Recruit, who is to be subsisted and sent back to the Continent at the Charge of the Hereditary Prince of or at that of the

Persons employed under his Serene Highness's Authority for recruiting these Corps.

I.

FORMATION of tbi Corps.

These Troops to be formed into Four Regiments of Infantiy, One Regiment of Chasseurs, Four Companies of Artillery, and One Company of Pioneers.

II. '

DISTRIBUTION of the Companies of Artillery Pioneers.

One of each of the Companies of Artillery' to be attached to each of the Regiments of Infantry, and the Company of Pioneers to the Corps of Chasseurs.-

III.

ESTABLISHMENT.

The Regiments of Infantry and Chasseurs, the Companies of Artillery and Pioneers, to consist of the Num-, bers expressed in Table No. I.

' IV.

ENGAGEMENT to he figrud by tie Recruit.

These Troops to take the Oath of Allegiance to His Majesty, and to serve in any Part of Europe His Majesty may think proper for the Term of Seven Years, and to lign an Engagement accordingly, and be liable to the same Regulations and Articles of War as His Majesty's British Troops.

V.

BOUNTY for the Men no<w at the Isle of Wight.

Each Non-commissioned Officer, Drummer, and Private now in the Isle of Wight, who shall be approved of and accepted for His Majesty's Service, to receive Two Pounds Ten Shillings as Bounty, out of which he must be provided with the Necessaries specified in the annexed No. II. the Remainder of the Bounty to be accounted for and paid to the Men; the Chasseur (or Yager) to have Three Pounds on Account of the Price of the Sac de Chafle.

VI.

RECRUITING Conditions in case of an Augmentation.

Whenever it shall be judged proper to complete or augment this Corps by Recruits from the Continent, the Hereditary Prince of Orange, or whoever under his Serene Highness's Authority may undertake to furnish such Recruits, only to enlist Men who have been in the Service of Holland, or who are natural born Subjects of the United Provinces, or belong to the Hereditary States of the Prince of Orange.

Vol. 55.

X.

PERIOD and CONDITIONS of tU Soldier's Difebttrge.

Each Man who shall serve his Time according to hia Engagement shall be entitled to his Discharge; and be Tent to the Continent, should he require it, with Two Months Pay (provided he has behaved during the Term of his Service properly) to carry him to his Home, Government to be at the Expence of taking him to the Continent should he be discharged in , or in any other insular Situation. The Two Months I^ay to date from the Day of his landing on the Continent, or in any Part of the United Provinces.

XI.

PROVISION for wounded or di fabled Non - commissioned Officers, Drummers^ and Privates.

In Cafes of Wounds, or long and faithful Services, the Non-commissioned Officers, Drummers, and Privates will be entitled to the same Treatment as Sol-

diers j or if they choose to return Home, they will re ceive a Sum of Money as a Reward for their Services, in the same Way as is now practiled with Foreign Soldiers in the Sixtieth Regiment, who prefer returning to the Continent to receiving a Pension in England.

XIJ.

No Soldier to be discharged but with the Knowledge of the Military Commissary.

During the Capitulation no Non-commissioned Officer, Drummer, or Private shall be discharged but with the Knowledge and Consent of the Military Commissary.

XIII.

E $JUIPMENT

Government to furnish Arms and Accoutrements.

XIV.

CLOTHING.

Complete Clothing will be delivered to each Corps for its effective Number, for which a Receipt will be given by the Commanding Officer of each Battalion, and for which Clothing he is to be responsible, and to account for its Issue Twice a Year, on the 24th of April and the 24th of October, making Returns of the fame,

together with the Return of the Arms and Accoutrements at those Periods, to the Secretary at War, and to the Military Commissary. It is clearly to be understood, that no Part of the Clothing is the Property of the

XV.

CAPTAINS responfihle for the Arm of tbtir Campania,

The Captains receiving an Allowance for keeping complete and in repair the Arms of their respective Companies, they are to replace such of them as may be lost or destroyed by wilful Neglect or Abuse.

XVI.

RATE tf Pap and Allowances,

The same Pay and Allowances to be granted to both Officers and Men, as to His Majesty's Infantry Regiments, in whatever Part of His Majesty's Dominions they may serve with them. The Particulars of this Pay and Allowance are annexed to the Establishment, numbered, I. No Difference of Pay to be made to the Artillery or Yagers.

XVII.

Eventual Alterations in the Pay and Allowances

In the Event of these Corps being employed on the Continent in Conjunction with any other Foreign Corps, His Majesty shall be at Liberty to place them on any Rate of Pay and Allowances granted to such Foreign Troops of the same Denomination with whom they may serve, as His Majesty shall think fit. Though the Pay and Allowances may from this Cause occasionally vary, ytt Jhe Mode and Period of making up and of giving in the Accounts are by no Means to be altered; and to prevent the Condition which may arise from too frequent Changes, no Alteration of Pay and Allowances shall take place but on the Twenty-fifth Day of each Calendar Month. This Article to fdrm Part of the Engagement to be signed by the Non-commissioned Officers, Drutp-mers, and Privates now at the Isle of Wight, who may be accepted for the King's Service; and by any Recruit hereafter to be enlisted, at the Time his Engagement is signed, the Twenty-third Article is also to be read to him.

XVIII.

DATE of Officers Commissions. t,

The Officers Commissions to bear Datejfrom the Day on which this Capitulation shall be signed; and the Officers belonging to the Corps, who shall be in England to receive British Pay from the 24th 1799.

XIX.

COMMENCEMENT of Pay to M a.

The Non-commissioned Officers, Drummers, and Privates now at the Isle of Wight, who shall be approved, to receive Pay from the Day on which this Capitulation is signed.

XX.

The Dutch Troops subjtd to say Variation in tie Pap and Allowances to the British Amy.

Whatever Variation of Pay or Regulation of interior (Economy His Majesty shall think proper to establish hereafter for the Government of the Troops, shall, in such Instances as the King shall think expedient be, extended to the Dutch Troops.

XXI.

Officers to join within Three Months,

All Officers to join within the Space of Three Months after the Date of their Commission; and if they do not join within that Period their Appointment to such Commissions to be considered void. No Officer is to receive Pay until he shall join the Corps.

XXII.

PROVISION for wounded Officers.

Officers rendered incapable of Service by Wounds, or other Infirmities contracted while in the Discharge of their Military Duty, and while in the British Service, to receive a Provision from this Country, in no same to exceed the Half Pay of the Rank they hold at the Time of being so incapacitated.

XXIII.

These Troops to pass into the Service of his Serene Highness the HeresBtasy Prince of Orange.

In the Event of the lawful Government of the United Provinces being restored, or his Serene Highness the

Stadtholder, or the Hereditary Prince of Orange being so situated in virtue of any Arrangements which may have received the Concurrence of His Majesty, as to be able to maintain and employ Viefe Troops on the Continent of Europe, they are to be held at his Serene High-

ness's DispofaJ, on his transmitting a Requisition to that Effect to the Secretary of State, and to the Commander in Chief for the Time being, Three Months previous to the Time at which the Troops are to quit His Majesty's Service.

XXIV.

Officers Commissions to he signed by His Royal Highness the Commander in Chief, and by his Serene Highness the Stadtholder.

All the Commissions in the Corps to be granted for the present by His Royal Highness the Commander in Chief, in the same Manner as they are now granted to the Officers of the other Foreign Corps, and these Officers to be also commissioned by the Stadtholder or Hereditary Prince of Orange-, which Commissions are to be of an equal Rank with those granted by His Royal Highness the Commander in Chief.

XXV.

Their Serene Highneffits the Prince, or the Hereditary Prince of Orange to recommend to Commissions.

His Serene Highness the Stadtholder or the Hereditary Prince of Orange to recommend to all the vacant Commissions. 1

XXVI.

PREFERENCE to the Dutch Officers receiving an Allowance.

The Officers formerly in the Service of Holland, and now receiving an Allowance from Great Britain, to be among the first Persons placed in this Corps.

XXVII.

MILITARY COMMISSARY.

A Military Commissary, who is also to act as Inspector, to be named to the Dutch Corps on their being received into the Service.

XXVIII.

PAYMASTER.

A Paymaster for the whole Corps, with Assistants to be attached to each of the separate Battalions, to be appointed by the Prince of Orange, but subject to the In-llruftions, Regulations, and Restrictions of the War Office, of which Copies are annexed.

XXIX.

His Strtnt Nights fslb Hertditarj tb Proprietor.

The Hereditary Prince'of Orange, with the Approbation of his Serene Highness the Stadtholder, to be.considered as Proprietor of the Whole of the Corps, and to enjoy Six Hundred Pounds for each Battalion of One Thousand Men, or Three Thousand Pounds pqr Annum for the present Corps.

XXX.

Colonel Commandant of Battalion of One Thousand Men.

To each Battalion of One Thousand Men shall be appointed a Colonel Commandant, whose Pay shall be made up Five Hundred Pounds per , without any further Emoluments: These Colonels Commandants, when with their Regiments, to be considered only as a Major General in the British Service not on the Staff, visiting his Regiment, and of course will not exercise a General Command over the other Corps, without receiving a special Power for that Purpose.

XXXI.

TheCHASSEURS.

The Yagers, although stated at Six Companies, are not to be considered as a Regiment, until their Numbers are increased so as to form Ten Companies of the Strength specified in the annexed Plan, at wfiich Time a Colonel Commandant may be recommended, with the proper Number of Officers.

A Message from the Lords, by Mr. Popham and Mr. Spranger:

Mr. Speaker,

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act to continue, until the First Day of January One thousand Eight hundred and Four, several Acts relating to the Admission of certain Articles of Merchandize in Neutral Ships, and to the issuing of Orders in Council for that Purpose; without any Amendment: And also.

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act for permitting the free Importation of Linseed Cakes and Rape Cakes in Neutral Ships; without any Amendment: And also.

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act for further continuing and amending an Act, made in the last Session of Parliament, for enabling His Majesty to prohibit the Exportation, and permit the Importation, of Com, and for allowing the Importation of other Articles of Provision without Payment of Duty; without any Amendment: And also.

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act to empower the Governor and Company of the Bank of England to purchase certain Houses and Ground contiguous to the Bank of England, and to enable them to improve certain Avenues adjacerst thereto; without any Amendment: And also.

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act for continuing fi r Twenty-one Years, and from thence to the End o! the then next Session of Parliament, the 9

Term, and altering and enlarging the Powers, of an Act, passed in the Seventeenth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, for more effectually amending, widening, and keeping in Repair, several Roads leading from the Market House, in the Town of Kidderminster, in the County of Worcester, and several other Roads therein mentioned; without any Amendment: And also,

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act for more effectually amending, widening, improving, and keeping in Repair, several Roads leading from the Hundred House, in the County of and also several

other Roads therein mentioned; without any Amendment: And also.

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act to enable Sir George Pigot, Baronet, Margaret and Frances Pigot, to dispose of a Diamond by a Lottery; with some Amendments; to which Amendments the Lords desire the Concurrence of this House: And also.

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act for dividing, allotting, and inclosing, the Commons and Waste Lands in the Parish of in the County of

Flint, and in the Parish of Nannetch, in the Counties of Flint and Denbigh; with some Amendments; to which Amendments the Lords desire the Concurrence of this House.

And then the Messengers withdrew.

Petition of A Petition of the several Persons, whose Names are Jo — , thereunto subscribed, being Journeymen and Workmen, tingham. residing in the Town and County of the Town of Nottingham, and the immediate Neighbourhood thereof, was presented to the House, and read; Taking Notice of an Act, made in the last Session of Parliament, to prevent unlawful Combinations of Workmen; and Setting forth. That, by the said Statute, directly or indirectly to attempt to prevail on any Journeyman or Workman to quit the Service in which he is employed, is declared illegal, the Breach of a Private Contraft in refuting to work when hired, is transformed into a criminal Offence, and in these and other Instances Acts of the moll equivocal Nature are made criminal by. Words of the most vague and indeterminate Construction, and are rendered punishable, at the absolute Discretion of Magistrates, by Fine and imprisonment, without the Intervention of a Jury, and without the Possibility of removing the Proceedings by Certiorari; and that, if the said Law should continue in force, it will be dangerous for the Petition-

3 0° Junii. _ A. 1800.

ers to converse with each other, and, as it will substitute Distrust and Jealously in the place of confidential Intercourse, it will have a Tendency to injure or destroy the Trades and Manufactures it profeffcs to protest And therefore praying. That the said Act may be repealed, or that the House will give such Relief in the Premises to the Petitioners as may seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of the Committee of the whole House, td whom it is referred to consider of the said Act.

of the Black Rod:

Mr. Speaker,

The Lords, authorized by virtue of His Majesty's Commission, for declaring His Royal Assent to several Acts agreed upon by both Houses, do desire the immediate Attendance of this Honourable House in the House of Peers, to hear the Commission read.

Accordingly Mr. Speaker, with the House, went up to the House of Peers.

And being returned;

Mr. Speaker reported. That the House, at the Desire of the Lords authorized by virtue of His Majesty's Commission afore-mentioned, had been at the House of Peers, where a Commission under the Great Seal was read, giving, declaring, and notifying the Royal Afifent to the several Public and Private Bills therein mentioned; and also empowering His Royal Highness the Prince of Wales, His Royal Highness the Duke of York, His Royal Highness the Duke of Clarence, His Royal Highness the Duke of Kent, -His Royal Highness the Duke of Cumberland, His Royal Highness the Duke of Gloucester, the Lord Archbishop of Canterbury, the Lord HighChan-cellor of Great Britain, and several other Lords, to de dare and notify the Royal Assent to the said Bills; and that the Lord High Chancellor of Great Britain, the Earl Kerr, and the Earl Spencer, named also in the said Commission, did accordingly declare and notify the Royal Assent to the said Bills: Which Bills are as followed; viz.

An Act to remove Doubts arising from the Construe-tion of an Act, made in the Thirty-ninth Year of His present Majesty's Reign, intituled, "An Act for permining certain Goods imported from the East Indies " to be warehoused, and for repealing the Duties now " payable thereon, and granting other Duties in lieu " thereof:"

An Act to allow, for Nine Months after the passing of the Act, the Use of Sugar in the brewing of Beer:

An Act to revive, and continue until the First Day of July One thousand Eight hundred and One, such Part of an Act, made in the present Session of Parliament, for reducing the Duties upon Spirits distilled from Me lasses or Sugar, or any Mixture therewith, and for other Purposes; as relates to the Duties on Wort or Wash brewed or made from Melaftes or Sugar:

An Act for further continuing and amending an Act, made in the last Session of Parliament, for enabling His Majesty to prohibit the Exportation, and permit the Importation, of Corn, and for allowing the Importation of other Articles of Provision without Payment of Duty: An Act for permitting the free Importation of Linked Cakes and Rape Cakes in Neutral Ships:

An Act to continue, until the First Day of January One thousand Eight hundred and Four, several Acts re-, lating to the Ad million of certain Articles of Merchandize in Neutral Ships, and to the iiluing of Orders in Council for that Purpose:

An Act to repeal so much of an Act, passed in the Second Year of King James the First, as prohibits the Use of Horse Hides in making Boots and Shoes; and for better preventing the damaging of Raw Hides and Skins in the flaying thereof:

An Act for repealing Part of the Duties and Drawbacks of Customs on Kid Skins imported, and the Exemption of imported Kid Skins from Excise Duty 0:1 being d re lied in Great Britain:

An Act toleflen the Duties on Wine and Spirits, the Produce of the British Settlement of The Cape of Good Hope, and to empower the Importers to land the-lame before Payment of the Duties of Excise, and to lodge the same in Warehouses, and to allow the same to be shipped, free of Duty, as Stores to be consumed on board Merchant Ships on their Voyages:

A Message from the Lords, by Mr. Hol/ord and Mr. Graves:

Mr. Speaker,

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act for repealing the Duties of Excise on Distilleries in Scotland, and on the Exportation of made Spirits from England to Scotland, and for granting other Duties in lieu thereof, and for altering, amending, and continuing, certain Acts of Parliament for the Regulation of Distilleries in Scotland; without any Amendment: And also.

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act for extending the Powers of the Commissioners named in an Act, made in this present Session of Parliament, intituled, "An Act for appointing Commissioners to put in Execution an Act of this Session of Parliament, intituled, An Act for continuing and granting to His Majesty a Duty on Pensions, Offices, and " Personal Estates, in England, Wales, and the Town of " Berwick upon Tweed, and certain Duties on Sugar, " Malt, Tobacco, and Snuff, for the Service of the Year " One thousand Eight hundred, together with those " named in Two former Acts for appointing Commisfioners of the Land Tax;" for indemnifying such Persons named in the said Act as have acted as Commissioners of the Land Tax, and for rendering valid certain Acts done by them; without any Amendment: And also.

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act for altering and amending an Act, made in the Thirty-fifth Year of His present Majesty's Reign, intituled, "An Act for making and maintaining a Navigable Canal from the Town and County of the Town of " ampton, to the City of New Sarum, in the County of " Wilts, with a Collateral Branch to Northam, within " the Liberties of the Town of Southampton;" without any Amendment: And also.

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act to discharge from a disputed and dormant Claim of the Public, several Estates belonging to the Right honourable William Carr Earl of Erroll, Lord High Constable of Scotland; without any Amendment: And also.

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act for amending several Acts for regulating the Price and Assize of Bread; with an Amendment; to which Amendment the Lords defiie the Concurrence of this House: And also,

Mr. Abbot reported from the Committee, appointed to draw up the Address to be presented to His Majesty, That the Committee had drawn up an Address accordingly, which they had directed him to report to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is a« followeth; viz,

Yol 55.

Most Gracious Sovereign,

We, Your Majesty's most dutiful and loyal Subjects, the Commons of Great Britain, in Parliament assembled, having taken into our Consideration the State of the Public Records of this Kingdom, and the Necessity of providing for the better Arrangement, Preservation, and more convenient Use of the fame, humbly beg Leave to lay before Your Majesty the Report of our Proceedings thereon; and to represent to Your Majesty, that in several of the principal Offices we have found the Public Records preserved with great Order and Regularity, and in some few with a Method and Care which are exemplary; but that, in many of the most important Offices, they are wholly unarranged, undeferibed, and unascertained; that some of them are exposed to Erasure, Alteration, and Embezzlement, and others are lodged in Places where they are daily perishing by Damp, or incurring a continual Rilk of Dcstruction by Fire.

A Period of nearly Seventy Years has elapsed since the last general Parliamentary Inquiry upon this Subject; and, during this Interval of Time, the Change which has taken place in the Language and written Character of Judicial Proceedings, as well as the large Accumulation of Materials which has been progressively superadded in every Department, have increased the Difficulties of methodizing the several Repositories, or applying their Contents to Purposes of practical Use.

In the Course of our Inquiry, we have found that many of the Public Buildings allotted to these Uses, and especially those Buildings which belong to Your Majesty's Exchequer in all its Branches, comprehending the An-tient Records and Muniments of the Rights and Possessions of the Crown, and the Vouchers and Accounts of the Public Revenues and Expenditure, are in a State so incommodious and insecure, as to require immediate Attention.

It has also appeared to us, that the salutary Measures heretofore adopted, by Your Majesty's Authority, for methodizing the Contents of some of the principal Repositories of Your Majesty's Records and Papers of State, might also be extended to many other Repositories, with Consequences highly beneficial to the Public Service.

And the same Motives which encouraged our Predecessors to intreat Your Majesty's Directions for printing the antient Records of Domesday and the Rolls of Parliament, have also induced us to submit to Your Majesty's Wisdom our Desire of extending the same Measure to other antient and valuable Monuments of our History, Laws, and Government.

Your faithful Commons do therefore most humbly beseech Your Majesty, that You will be graciously pleased to give such Directions as Your Majesty, in Your great Wisdom, shall think fit, for the better Preservation, Arrangement, and more convenient Use, of the Public Records of this Kingdom.

And we beg Leave further to assure Your Majesty, that whatever extraordinary Expences may be incurred by the Directions which Your Majesty, in Your great Wisdom, shall think fit to give on this Occasion, shall be cheerfully provided for and made good by Yout faithful Commons.

The said Address being read a Second Time;

Resolved, That this House doth agree with the Com1 mittee in the said Address to be presented to His Majesty.

Ordered, That the said Address be presented to His Majesty by such Members of this House as are of His Majesty's most Honourable Privy Council.

Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer acquainted the King's Mcf-F(ouse, That he had a Message from His Majesty to this House, signed by His Majesty; and he presented the the Emperor, same to the House; and it was read by Mr. Speaker (all the Members of the House being uncovered); and is as followeth; viz.

GEORGE R.

His Majesty thinks it proper to lay before this House, the Copy of a Treaty which has been signed at Vienna, between His Majesty's Minister to that Court, and the Minister Plenipotentiary of the Emperor of Germany, duly authorized for that Purpose.

His Majesty has directed His Ratification of this Treaty to be immediately prepared, and transmitted to Vienna, to be exchanged in due Form with that of the Emperor; but, on Account of the present advanced Period of the Year, His Majesty has thought it belt not to delay communicating to Parliament the Engagements thus entered into; and He recommends it to this House, to adopt such Measures as may be necessary, in order to enable His Majesty to fulfil them.

His Majesty doubts not that He shall fee, in the Conduct of Parliament, in this Conjuncture, an additional Example of that good Faith, Firmness, and Determination, which have uniformly actuated the Councils of this Country; and Fie is persuaded, that His Parliament will concur with Flim in thinking, that, by furnishing the Means for prosecuting the War with Vigour, they best promote the Attainment of Peace, on Grounds

Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer presented to the House, by His Majesty's Command,

Copy of Convention between His Majesty,

and his Majesty the Emperor of the Romans, signed at Vienna, the 20th June 1800 — and Trandation.

And the Titles of the said Papers were read.

The Copy of the said Convention is preserved amongd the other Papers of this Session; and the said Trandation is as followeth viz.

TRANSLATION of a Convention between His Majesty and the Emperor of the Romans, signed at Vienna, the 20th June 1800.

His Majesty the Emperor of the Romans, King of Hungary and Bohemia, and His Majesty the King of Great Britain, have judged, that it was conformable to the Intered of their Crowns, and to the good of the Common Caul'c, to concert with each other on the bed Manner of giving Effect to the Union of their Efforts against the Common Enemy, in the present Campaign } in consequence of which the Baron de Tkugut, Grand Cross of the Order of St. Stephen, his Imperial Majesty's Minider of Conferences, and Commissary General and Minider Plenipotentiary in his Provinces of Italy, IJlria, and Dalmatia, See. and the Right honourable Gilbert Lord Minto, Peer of Great Britain, One of His Britannick

Majesty's Mod honourable Privy Council, and His Envoy Extraordinary and Minider Plenipotentiary to the Court of Vienna, being furnillied on the Part of their aforesaid Imperial and Britannick Majesties, with the Powers requisite for discussing and arranging this important Object. The said Plenipotentiaries after having respectively exchanged their full Powers, have agreed upon the following Articles:

Article I.

In order to relieve the pressing Necessities of the Finances of his Imperial Majesty, under the enormous Expences already incurred, and which remain to be incurred during the present Campaign, His Britannick Majesty shall advance to his above mentioned Imperial Majesty, by Way of Loan, the Sum of Two Million Pounds Sterling; this Sum shall be divided into Three Parts, and paid at Three different Periods, preferably in Specie, so that the Fird Third, of £.666,666. 13^. 4 shall be paid in the Fird Days of the Month of July, the Second Third of the like Sum in the Fird Days of September; and the remaining Third in the Fird Days of the Month of December.

Article II.

During the whole Continuance of the War, and during the Six Months which shall follow the Conclusion of a Peace between Austria and France, his Imperial Majesty Iliad not be bound to pay any Intered upon the Sum of Two Millions advanced, as dipulated in the preceding Article: Great Britain consenting to take this Charge upon her own Account until the Period above mentioned; but on the Expiration of the Term of Six Months after the Conclusion of Peace, his Imperial Majesty shall pay for the future to the British Government, or to the Individuals who shall be pointed out by the

British Government, an annual Rent, or annual Rents, making altogether the Amount of the Intereds of the

O o

Two Millions advanced; which Intereds shall be calculated at the same Rate, as the Intereds of the Loan

made on Account of the British Government in the pre-> sent Year. His Imperial Majesty shall moreover pay An- nually to the British Government, the Sum of £.20,000 Sterling, at Two Periods, that is to say, £.10,000 every Six Months; which Sum shall be employed in the l'uc-ccfiive Purchase and Reduction of the Principals of the Two Millions, according to the Method adopted by the British Government in its own Loans.

Article III.

Their Impcrialand Britannick Majesties mutually promise each other to carry on the War against the French Republic during the present Campaign, with all possible Vigour, and to employ in it all their respective Means by Land and Sea, concerting together as Occasion shall require, on the most advantageous Manner of reciprocally employing their Forces by Land and Sea, to the support of their Operations against the Common Enemy. H is Imperial Majesty shall be careful to complete his Armies of Germany and of Italy, in Proportion to the Lodes which they have fudained, in order always as far as possible to act against the Common Enemy, the same Number of effective Men conformably to the Statements-which his Imperial Majesty caused to be confidentially Communicated to the British Government, on the opening of the Campaign.

Article IV.

The Bavarian Troops, those of and the

Szvifs Regiments, in the Pay of Great Britain, shall be at the Disposition of his Imperial Majesty, to form a Part of his Army in Germany, and to be employed there in Operations against the Enemy, in Conformity to the Conventions and Capitulations concluded on this subject by the King of Great Britain: His Britannick Majesty shall take the necessary Measures for the further Reinforcement of the Army of his Imperial Majesty in Germany, by as great a Number as possible of German and Swiss Troops.

Article V.

Their Imperial and Britannick Majesties engage during the whole Continuance of the present Convention, not to make a separate Peace with the French Republic; without the previous and express Consent of each other. They engage likewil'e not to treat with the Enemy, nor to receive from him any Overtures either for a private Peace, or for a general Pacification, without making, mutually, Communications of them with Opennels, and aiding in every Respect.in perfect Concert.

Article VI.'

The Duration of the present Convention is fixed for the Term of One Year, to be computed from the id of March 1800, until the End of February 1801. From the Month of December, and immediately after the Acquittal of the lad Payment of the dipulated Advances, the Two High contracting Parties shall enter into Deliberation and confidential Explanation, upon the Determinations that they may think necessary to adopt for the future, according to Circumstances and their mutual Convenience.

Article VII.

The present Convention shall be ratified in due Form by their Imperial and Britannick Majesties, and the respective Ratifications diall be exchanged at Vienna, in the Space of Six Weeks, or sooner, if possible.

In Witness whereof. We, the undersigned, furnished with the full Powers of their Imperial and Britannick Majesties, have, in their Names, signed the present Convention, and have affixed thereunto the Seal of our Arms.

Done at Vienna, the Twentieth of June, in the Year 1800.

(L. S.) Le Baron de Thugut.(L. S.) Minto.

Ordered, That the said Papers do lie upon the Table, to be peruled by the Members of the House.
