Mr. Long accordingly reported from the said Committee, the Resolutions which the Committee bad directed to be reported to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same were read; and are as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That there be given on every Barrel of Superfine Wlteaten Flour of One Hundred and Ninety-six Pounds Weight, which shall be imported into Great Britain in any Ship which shall have cleared out from any Port in America between the 12th Day of November 1800 and the 10th Day of January 1801, and shall be lcld by Public Sale by Auction within Two Months alter Importation, a Bounty equal to the Sum by which the actual Price of each Barrel of such Flour l'o iold shall be less than Eighty Shillings.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That there be given on every Barrel of Fine Wheaten Flour of One Hundred and Ninety-six Pounds Weight, which shall be imported into Great Britain in any Ship which shall have cleared out from any Port in America between the 12th Day of November 1800 and the 10th Day of January 1801, and shall be sold by Public Sale by Auction within Two Months after Importation, a Bounty equal to the Sum by which the actual Price of each Barrel of such Flour to fold shall be Ids than Seventy-eight Shillings.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That there be given on every Barrel of Superfine Wheaten Flour, of One Hundred and Ninety-six Pounds Weight, which shall be imported into Great Britain in any Ship which shall have cleared out front any Port in America between the iotli Day of January and the 25th Day of March 1801, and shall be sold by Public Sale by Auction within Two Months after Importation, a Bounty equal to the Sum by which the actual Price of each Barrel of such Flour l'o fold shall be less than Ninety Shillings.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That there be given on every Barrel of Fine Flour, of One Hundred and Ninety-six Pounds Weight, which shall be imported into Great Britain in any Ship which shall have cleared out from any Port in America between the 10th Day of January and the 25th Day of March 1801, and shall be sold by Public Sale by Auction within Two Months after Importation, a Bounty equal to the Sum by which the actual Price of each Barrel of such Flour so fold shall be less than Eighty-eight Shillings.

A Message from His Majesty, by Sir Francis neux. Gentleman Usher of the Black Rod:

Mr. Speaker,

The King commands this Honourable House to attend His Majesty, immediately, in the House of Peers.

Accordingly Mr. Speaker, with the House, went up to attend His Majesty; where His Majesty was pleased to give the Royal Assent to the several Public and Private Bills following; viz.

An Act for raising a certain Sum of Money, by Loans or Exchequer Bills, for the Service of the Year One thousand Eight hundred and One, and for appropriating the Supplies granted in this Session of Parliament:

After which, His Majesty was pleased to make a most Gracious Speech from the Throne, to both Houses of Parliament; as followeth; viz.

My Lords, and Gentlemen,

I cannot suffer this Session to close without returning you My particular Acknowledgements for the distinguished Industry and Zeal with which you have applied yourselves to the interesting Object which, at the Commencement of the Session, I most especially recommended to your Attention.

It has been My earnest Wish that nothing should be omitted which could tend to relieve the Pressure occasioned by the present Dearth of Provisions, and to in-lure a sufficient Supply till the Produce of the next Harvest can be brought into Use.

The Diligence with which your Inquiries have been conducted has afforded you the belt Means of ascertaining the true Circumstances of Our present Situation; and the extensive Measures which you have wifely adopted in consequence, fordiminishing the Consumption of Grain, and procuring an encrealed Supply, will,

I doubt not, be found productive of the most salutary Effect.

Much, however, must depend on the Disposition which will, I am confident, be manifested by all those who have the Means of carrying into Execution My solemn Recommendation and Injunction, ill'ued at your Desire, for the Adoption of all practicable Economy in the Use of those Articles which are necessary to the Subsistence of the poorer Clafl'es of My Subjects.

The Time fixed for the Commencement of the Union of Great Britain and Ireland necessarily terminates your Proceedings on this important Subject; but I am persuaded that the Consideration of it will be resumed with the same Zeal and Temper on the First Meeting of the Parliament of the United Kingdom.

The early Period which I have appointed for that Meeting will afford a speedy Opportunity of completing whatever you may have necessarily left unfinished, and of considering what Measures may tend further to alleviate the Pressure on My People, or to prevent the Danger of its Recurrence.

Gentlemen of the House of Commons,

I thank you for the Readiness with which you have granted the Supplies neccliaty, under the present Cir cumstances, for the Public Service.

My Lords, and Gentlemen,

The Detention of the Property of My Subjects in the Ports of Russia, contrary to the most solemn Treaties, and the Imprisonment of Sailors in that

Country, have excited in Me Sentiments, in which you ana all My Subjects will, I am sure, participate. I have already taken stich Steps as this Occasion'indif-penfably required, and it will afford Me great Satisfaction if they prove effectual: But if it shall become necessary to maintain, against any Combination, the Honour and Independence of the British Empire, and those Maritime Rights and Interests on which both Our Prosperity and Our Security must always depend, 1 entertain no Doubt either of the Success of those Means which, in such an Event, 1 shall be enabled to exert, or of the Determination of My Parliament and My People to afford Me a Support proportioned to the Importance of the Interests which We have to maintain.

And afterwards the Lord Chancellor, by His Ma^ jetty's Command, said.

My Lords, and Gentlemen,

It is His Majesty's Command, that the Proclamation, declaring His Majesty's most Gracious Intention, that the Members of Parliament composing this Parliament should be the Members of the Parliament of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland on the Part of Great Britain, and that the said Parliament should be afi'embled on the 2 2d Day of January next, be delivered in full Parliament, and now read, which closes the present Session.
